Okay, I will preface this review by saying I have spent 10hr+ on this game and plan to spend even more than that before I am finished. The first dishonored was bar none one of my absolute favorite games. If you love stealth games and a good challenge every once in a while, then this is your game. One of the biggest things I love about this game and the first one is that it is a play your way type thing. If you want to sneak through the levels unseen, you can try that. If you want to run around killing everyone/ thing you see HEY you can do that too.
For me the story was not as gripping in this games as it was in the first. It was, nonetheless, interesting all the same. I do like that they lengthened the amount of time that the story takes to play out. If you're not sure if you'll enjoy this game or not I would tell you to buy the first one, it is only 10 bones after all. If you like the first one do not hesitate to pick this one up too. It is pretty much everything you love about the first one with a better engine and sharper graphics.
One last thing some people have complained about poor optimization for PC but I have had no problem running 1080p a 60fps.
PC Specs:
I7 6700k
ASUS GTX 970
16 gb ram
250gb ssd
2tb hard disk

----------------------
Story/Lore (SPOILERS!)
----------------------
Very insuring lore and very nice steampunk theme. The world has mass amount of lore behind it with such things as diseases that occurred during the times, famous people that made very futuristic things, and stories on what happened to people in that time era. The story happens about 20 or so years later after the first Dishonored so expect to play as Corvo or Emiley and not see one of them for most of the game, because you have to pick one. The story does not best the first but is still a very good story with interesting characters and enemies, cool interactions with other NPCs and constant interactions with the Outsider. There is more to be told in this game about the Outsider more than the first had which is quite good for the lore.
8/10 For Lore and Story Telling
----------------------
Gameplay (Hard Difficulty)
----------------------
Very similar gameplay to the first with harder stealth that filled that gap it had in the first one. New types of enemies which can not be stealth killed (Clock Tower Soldiers) and depending on who you pick between Emily and Corvo your powers. Between Emily and Corvo's Outsider given powers they have similar ones (Blink, Dark Vision, Validity, Shadow Kill exc.) but also a lot of different ones as well (Doppelganger, Stealth Form, Far Reach, and Domino) while Corvo has his classics. This game can be played how you want to be played and it says that in the game it supports stealth to full out just sword and gun fights. The stealth is a little better because you can now kill enemies over cover and under cover such things as the first did not.
9/10 For Gameplay
----------------------
Graphics/Optimization (Max Settings)
----------------------
This game has a very colorful and beautiful city and is easy on the eyes. There are not a lot of extra Nvidia Workshop settings you would expect from a Nvidia sponsored game but there are some. The port however is yes you guessed it♥♥♥♥♥♥at the moment but I am not marking down the score for that because they said they are fixing the problem soon. The graphics on everything look well detailed and very well textured, very smooth and has a cartoon like theme to the graphics which works as well. The models I do have to say look a little weird in my opinion. It's just the way they look such as their bodies and faces but its not bad, just the artstyle.
8/10 For graphics (Port is going to be fixed)
----------------------
Final Score:8.3 Should have added some new gameplay mechanics, but at the end of the day still a great game for the series.
----------------------

I got this game in some kind of bundle a long time ago. I recently (summer 2017) decided to play a few minutes just to get a sense of the lore and environment before moving on to Wasteland 2 (and in the future, Wasteland 3)
I was completely hooked: This is one of the better RPG:s I've played. I did play a lot in the 90s, but this game is old even in my standards so it isn't just nostalgia speaking.
It is an older game, which means:
* Bad inventory system. You don't want to make too much changes because it takes forever to reorganize stuff
* Auto-saves on each new area. Back up your save files manually at least after each play session or major milestone so you don't end up in a bad state with all your characters dead.
* Keep a lot of notes of the clues and directions you get in the game. You will not have a quest log or similar to help you along the way.
* To heal your characters, you need to either visit a doctor or put something over the ESC key (pass time) while you go get a glass or water or taking a bathroom break. Also, permadeath if you mess up. (So you'd better have those save files stashed away!)
BUT:
* The story and world is interesting and enjoyable
* The characters you meet are diverse and well-written
* The gameplay is fun and interesting
* Mullets galore and names like "Angela Deth" and "Hell Razor"
Definitely recommend.

My initial thoughts after playing TESO for roughly 8 hours (see futher down for my extended review while I have put now more than 30 hours in)
I was a skeptic of TESO due to a lackluster beta experience and many negative reviews that accompanied the release. Like others I decided to not purchase this game. I decided to bite the bullet this week when it launched on steam for 50% off the standard edition. I am so glad that I did because I am having a great time with TESO. The graphics, music, quest system, voice acting are some of the best in the industry. Some of the quests involving The Prophet send chills through my body because the sound effects mixed with rich grahics and voice acting really do bring you deep into the game. TESO offers many different character and class customizations where it makes you feel like you have total control over the advancement of your skills and stats. Crafting and gathering are also important components of the gameplay as I have found they fill the gaps in your gear. In the open world Anchors are fun public battles that randomly pop up; I found these fun, challenging, and rewarding.
TESO is a subscription based game with the first 30 days free. Some have described a lacking end game in TESO which I have not reached yet. There are some expected overhauls coming down the pipeline according to the Devs at Quakecon14 so I will stay tuned. My strategy will be to play the hell out of this awesome game. If needed I will unsubscribe and wait for updates if some of what I read is true about the end game. Until then I will continue my Epic journey in TESO.
In summary TESO offers all the RPG elements that are expected of a modern video game. I can not say enough how epic my journey has been thus far and how pleased I am with the graphics and sound. If you are a fan of the Elder Scrolls world; Skyrim or the like there of, I would highly suggest giving this at least a play through. While the sale is now over, I'm sure there will be another one so keep an eye out.
Extended Review I 7/23 (Almost 24 hours played):
I chose the Dominion faction to begin my TESO journey, and I really enjoyed the starting continent. The exploration in TESO is really good. Literally every corner of the continent is worth travelling to because of all the different quests, dungeons, and elite battles that you will encounter. The rewards are worth it too because you can find skyshards which are scattered and typically hidden. Obtain 3 shards and you gain a skill point. This is really helpful with your character's progression. When I hit level 10 I was summoned once again by The Prophet. The epic quest resumed and I have to say so far this is my favorite aspect of the quest system of TESO.
I aslo did my first party dungeon. Players were waiting outside of the entrance and eager to fill in the 4 man groups to begin. The dungeon was challenging and had 5 bosses all with unique abilities. Most of the battles were not easy at first but not too difficult to figure out. One thing to note, once you exit or complete the dungeon you can do it again as many times as you want. The loot was also notable with most bosses dropping blue rarity gear and some greens.
I hope you enjoyed the review, I will keep adding to it :)
Extended Review II 7/26/14 (30+ hours played):
I'm still hooked to the game and I just hit level 24 on my Woodelf Nightblade who uses Medium Armor, Bow, and a mixture of Siphon and Shadow abilities. I just cleared the Grahtwood zone which is the second area for the Dominion faction. The quests are all interesting and do not feel repetitive. While some of the solo dungeons seem similar in layout they are not 100% the same so that really helps because I was worried they would become kinda like a template. I also just finished the level 20 group dungeon EH which went by smooth with only 1 boss wipe for the group. I would say so far the difficulty is right on par for a well balanced group consisting of 1 tank, 1 healer and 2 DPS. I really do enjoy exploring the map in it's entirety and reading all of the books I find. I noticed you even get skill gains off of some books which adds value to taking the time to look at them.
8.5/10 (30+ hours played)

I'll not spend too much time echoing what others have said.  Instead, I'll draw your attention to a key choice the game has you focus on:
As you can see from the official trailer, Alice Ivers has type 1 diabetes and will die if she doesn't get her insulin.  Getting that insulin is something close to a full time job.  You have complete control over Alice and could easily march her off into the desert to die.  Or you grit your teeth, double down, and get one more syringe to get through one more day.
It's honestly a tough call, and you don't find decisions like that in games these days.
Good stuff.

As a new comer to indie games, I was slightly skepticle about spending the $5 for it.  Thankfully there is a demo available for it, and after I played the demo, I was sold.  Best way to describe Sruvivalist would be a "post apocalyptic, zombie survival, base building, resource gathering goodness".  While the graphics may not be "top of the line", and the camera cannot zoom in or out(same with minimap), and at the moment; there really are only three guns available(been unable to locate the sniper rifle if it is in game yet; found plenty of ammo but no gun,  the gameplay itself is very solid.  The music is well made, and the idea of being able to improve relations with various survivor groups around you to possiably recruit them later is very nice.  On top of the basic find food, water, guns and ammo, the devs also included a twist of one of the survivors you find that joins up with you, needs insuline b/c they are type-1 diabetic; resulting in some nail biting moments when running to the nearest trader in hopes they have some left for sale to save her life.
Melee is fun, but much more enjoyable when using a fire arm.  Filling a zombie with lead and then kicking them away is entertaining as well as if the slo-mo kills get combined into it.  One of my personal favorite things they did for this game is to allow you to build your own base (once you find a survivor that can help build, but they are near by in the beginning ;) ).  Base building can seem pretty straight forward, build a wall here, gate there, tower over here, shack over there.  However, to build the base, you need supplies, aka lumber, chicken wire, cement, ect ect ect.  This causes you to either just let one person build, than go out alone to gather supplies(which will only be one of each since the mats weigh so much), or send out a few ppl to gather the mats, so the builder can stay safely tucked away in the base and they can protect each other?  Mean while, you can keep exploring and looting.  Also enjoy the fact that you can start growing your own food and make a well, creating a self sufficent base.
Sometimes while exploring you will find small camps of looters, that want nothing more than what you have, and they will attack.  A nice feature is sometimes, one of them will surrender, and offer to join you if you wish, leaving you the choice to take them in, take all of their stuff, or kill them.  Many npcs will have quests, and there are a few times where "things are not as they seem" with the quest, adding to the depth of the game.  There are so many positive things that can be said about this game they greatly reduce or destroy any negativity I may have about it.  It is after all, a indie game.  For $5, you get more out of it than many $20 + games made by reconized labels.  I'd have no qualms about spending $10 for this game. I'd highly recommend this game to any one, and if you are unsure, check out the demo first.

sure doesn't skimp on the story. In the first half an hour alone, you can find twenty long correspondences relaying the back plot, scrawled out in dainty long-winded chickenscratch. By the time you've left the relatively normal surroundings of the manor, you'll have read what feels like the equivalent of a novella. I'm certainly not going to complain about such great effort going into a game's lore but the pacing of it may instantly turn a lot of players away; there are instances where you read a long journal entry from the house cook, only to walk two feet and run into another full page from the maid, an issue compounded by the fact that very little actually happens in the beginning aside from poking through drawers and garbage to find keys or lock combinations.
It's a decent game so far but I'd urge caution for more traditional fans of the genre. It's far too lethargic to rustle up any sort of fear factor or tension at this point, leaving you with the equivalent of an old ghost story that has fallen out of relevance with today's more steely-nerved audience.
My wanderings below:

For an Early Access game, this stands head and shoulders above a lot of others. It's not perfect, but that's what Early Access is for, right?
We pay for the right to Beta test and get some face time with the devs, and tell them what we think, and where they might go about doing things a little differently. Yes?
Excellent.
Now for the fun part. I wasn't sure what to make of this on the store page prior to release, as they had a few bits of war footage, a creepy-looking run-down/abandoned house, and such. Reminded me more of 7th Guest than Amnesia, if we're being honest. Then again, I saw more of Amnesia in videos than I did playing it.
I spent a half-hour with this game, and what I saw was the look and feel of 7th Guest with the gameplay of Gone Home. I rated the latter hard in my review of it, primarily because it was simplistic, walky, and full of bits and bobs that didn't seem to have a lot to do with one another.
Not so the first area of this game. The world is fully realized, and you can see the love and care that went into setting the  stage in a rather creepy mansion. The various bits of the environment are blended together nicely, and it almost feels like you're in post-WWI France (or maybe Germany, the exact location isn't particularly clear). The missing people here make it clear that soemthing went on, and that they left for what they considered a real reason-- not that they were out for a few hours away from their puzzle-trap.
The puzzles make sense in context, and what you're looking for in one area may be in another area that you still have access to. A very early puzzle requires that you find a couple of objects, and *then* you can work out the main puzzle in one room while the clues to solve it are in another entirely. They're not brain-breakers, but they're certainly enough to keep you exploring all the nooks and crannies while trying to solve them.
There are lots of bits of paper floating around, but mostly they're just background. They do help, but they're not strictly necessary. There will probably be an achievement for getting them all, but you don't *have* to have them if you feel like floundering around for awhile.
It's stagecraft. Very nice stagecraft if you're someone like me that adores story, but if you just want to power through, you can go without. I recommend getting as many as you can the first playthrough and trying for a speedrun after that.
Now for the Bad Things, and I only really have two:
First, turning the texture quality down will definitely impact your ability to play. That first puzzle I mentioned won't work if you're using low-quality textures. I tried that, and had to turn them up to see what I was doing. Once I returned them to the default (high), it was doable. If you don't have a more modern rig, you might want to give it a pass, or at least turn them up for a few minutes while you work through puzzles that require you read things.
My three-year-old laptop tolerated it, but it was kind of a near thing. Same of the shadows: at lower quality setting, they're a murky green color, but set to default, they work well.
There was a bug with an inventory puzzle at the end of my playthrough, and that was with a thing that didn't return to the inventory when commanded. Not sure what that was about.
Now for the other thing, and this one was a problem (for me): The graphic settings allow you to change the quality of the experience, and well done, but there are no options to change the resolution. I tend to play games at 1600x900 Windowed so I can look at other things that might need addressing, whereas this game really loves to run Fullscreen. You can window it, but it retains that 1920x1080 frame size, and it cannot be adjusted. Your mileage may vary, but I found it rather irksome.
As stated at the top of the review, this is an Early Access title, and the Dev says they want to make sure they've got all the bugs out before they finish things. Sincerely, I hope they do. For all my griping in the last couple of paragraphs, it's a solid start to what looks to be a really interesting game. For the full price, it's not a bad deal. For the intro price of $5.99, it's very nearly a steal.
Well done, Triple Brick. Well done.
You're welcome to contact me about any specifics, and I can show you the footage with the issues I had, and maybe a few ways you might resolve them.
TL;DR: Fun little creep-out in an environment that makes sense and isn't overloaded with oppressive music loops. I'll wander back and append more to this as I get further through the game.

First and foremost. This is a Classic, I even enjoyed it once I got past the "everyone dies far too often stage".  Would I recommend it for any other purpose than "you should have played it"? No, it's an utter nightmare to play and that issue stands even more now than back in 1988. So Recommend Yes/No gets a 51% thumbs up ;)
If you still think you should suffer through it, I'll explain my comment. With proper guidance you can enjoy it (and without you will probably play it 2-3 times longer than required).
I played through every RPG I could gethold of back in the CMB64/early PC days and finished almost all. I would like to say all the Ultimas, Bard's tales, AD&D etc were completed but Wasteland... it was the first RPG I even gave up on.  Followed by Ultima IX because it was a buggy action adenture with millimeter movement and Ultima Underworlds because for some reason they bored me to death.
So what was wrong with Wasteland? Spoilers warning, although very minimal!
Insanely difficult without extra help. No internet and a 300baud modem wasn't worth enough. So I died from radiation, heat exhaustion, not enough safe places to rest, certainly never had enough Medics (or managed to walk to Doctors in time), always run out of ammo and finally tossed the entire♥♥♥♥♥♥game when I met the Scorpitron (the Vegas nightmare if I remembered the name wrong :) ).
This time I almost tossed it out after beating bunnies forever right at the beginning. But I figured I will do it with a walkthrough and minimize time spent suffering. And I'm glad I did, the story is great and once you get to doctor stages and finally some decent armour it's almost fun.
But I STILL suffered. After 33h of play to complete it I will list some of the noticeable annoyances. Veterans will laugh at some and hopefully not nod at the last one.
Oh, and I'm a packrat. So I almost hauled every knife to a shop (ok, not in THIS game). That explains why it took so long. Oh, and my characters never die, EVER. Except in this game, good riddance.
The horrors:
1) Save and save often (and take backups of your saves). I didn't actually have to revertto saves all that often (except with the Scorpitron and on more place I cannot remember)  After hitting a mine twice in two moves in Vegas and losing Ace and not realizing it before saving the next time I considered going back a few hours in saves but naaaah.
2) Not enough ammo, ever. Yes, I actually run out of 7.62 clips around Vegas so I had to chainsaw a while. My own fault, packrat and not wanting to switch weapons styles according to ammo.
3) Half working macros. Well, without macros I would never EVER have played through this nightmare. Unfortunatley they had some cutting off limit so with 7 characters the last character had to evade to get proper A1S etc combos for the first 6. Only 1 single character left at that point :(
4) You can apparently drop crucial items and the game become impossible to complete. There were a few items I could never find again even though I always sold stuff to be sure. The Darwin upper shop closed forever at some point though so maybe my stuff was there.
5) At the end I needed two plasma couplers and there was only one in Cochise. The walkthrough said there should be one more on robots outside but never found one. I actually had to GRIND my characters up two levels to get 3 skill points into IQ and get Toaster repair. If I would have ended up with unplayable at that stage I would have tossed the damn thing or tried to hack items. Seriously, sheeeesh.
6) And the biggie. Finishing off the game at 1 am (yes, it was good enough for a 2-3 last late run)... and I apparently made it unfinisable and had to revert to a save 2h earlier (famous words: "not much left, just do it"). Why? When doing the last cylinder the game popped up some message and I hit space (being tired and all). After which I was locked away in a small room and that was it. I pretty much always played with a full party as I just wanted to finish the damn thing off. So the final solution was a really NASTY one. In 1988 without help and no disk scumming saves I think I would have forced the disk down Fargo's throath at that point.
Ok, there you have it, suffer if you want but I really recommend a walkthrough because the game is so aged suffering just because of the good story simply isn't worth it. And one mistake 10h before the finish might leavy you hanging if you happen to drop something crucial by mistake.

My initial thoughts after playing TESO for roughly 8 hours (see futher down for my extended review while I have put now more than 30 hours in)
I was a skeptic of TESO due to a lackluster beta experience and many negative reviews that accompanied the release. Like others I decided to not purchase this game. I decided to bite the bullet this week when it launched on steam for 50% off the standard edition. I am so glad that I did because I am having a great time with TESO. The graphics, music, quest system, voice acting are some of the best in the industry. Some of the quests involving The Prophet send chills through my body because the sound effects mixed with rich grahics and voice acting really do bring you deep into the game. TESO offers many different character and class customizations where it makes you feel like you have total control over the advancement of your skills and stats. Crafting and gathering are also important components of the gameplay as I have found they fill the gaps in your gear. In the open world Anchors are fun public battles that randomly pop up; I found these fun, challenging, and rewarding.
TESO is a subscription based game with the first 30 days free. Some have described a lacking end game in TESO which I have not reached yet. There are some expected overhauls coming down the pipeline according to the Devs at Quakecon14 so I will stay tuned. My strategy will be to play the hell out of this awesome game. If needed I will unsubscribe and wait for updates if some of what I read is true about the end game. Until then I will continue my Epic journey in TESO.
In summary TESO offers all the RPG elements that are expected of a modern video game. I can not say enough how epic my journey has been thus far and how pleased I am with the graphics and sound. If you are a fan of the Elder Scrolls world; Skyrim or the like there of, I would highly suggest giving this at least a play through. While the sale is now over, I'm sure there will be another one so keep an eye out.
Extended Review I 7/23 (Almost 24 hours played):
I chose the Dominion faction to begin my TESO journey, and I really enjoyed the starting continent. The exploration in TESO is really good. Literally every corner of the continent is worth travelling to because of all the different quests, dungeons, and elite battles that you will encounter. The rewards are worth it too because you can find skyshards which are scattered and typically hidden. Obtain 3 shards and you gain a skill point. This is really helpful with your character's progression. When I hit level 10 I was summoned once again by The Prophet. The epic quest resumed and I have to say so far this is my favorite aspect of the quest system of TESO.
I aslo did my first party dungeon. Players were waiting outside of the entrance and eager to fill in the 4 man groups to begin. The dungeon was challenging and had 5 bosses all with unique abilities. Most of the battles were not easy at first but not too difficult to figure out. One thing to note, once you exit or complete the dungeon you can do it again as many times as you want. The loot was also notable with most bosses dropping blue rarity gear and some greens.
I hope you enjoyed the review, I will keep adding to it :)
Extended Review II 7/26/14 (30+ hours played):
I'm still hooked to the game and I just hit level 24 on my Woodelf Nightblade who uses Medium Armor, Bow, and a mixture of Siphon and Shadow abilities. I just cleared the Grahtwood zone which is the second area for the Dominion faction. The quests are all interesting and do not feel repetitive. While some of the solo dungeons seem similar in layout they are not 100% the same so that really helps because I was worried they would become kinda like a template. I also just finished the level 20 group dungeon EH which went by smooth with only 1 boss wipe for the group. I would say so far the difficulty is right on par for a well balanced group consisting of 1 tank, 1 healer and 2 DPS. I really do enjoy exploring the map in it's entirety and reading all of the books I find. I noticed you even get skill gains off of some books which adds value to taking the time to look at them.
8.5/10 (30+ hours played)

I admit, originally when i saw this game i thought 'This is a nice concept though it doesn't seem very well executed, also looks kind of strange'. I bought the game thinking 'Might as well give it a try'. I played the game on the edge of my chair trying to keep my survivors alive for just another day. I still haven't stopped playing this game(I'm actually trying to complete a quest as i type this).
Overall, this game is a fresh & interesting combination between a classic topdown zombie survival game, Sims & The Walking Dead.
Pros:
Not purely quest-driven. I've played more than my fair share of zombie games that are 'Go get X object, return the object to Y person, get Z reward and progress in the game'. Survivalist does away with the linear quest-driven system & replaces it with a nice 'Go do it if you want to, or if you don't just don't. We're not going to hold anything away from you if you don't'.
If you're told 'Go and stop this gang' then you also have the choice of assimilating into your group/community instead of just marching in there & murdering everyone
A unique relationship system. Instead of the standard 'i like you, i don't' Survivalist has a twin-axis system of respect and approval. You can make someone do what you want by either making them like you, or fear you. They see you burn their village to the ground single-handedly then they'll fear you, if you save them from being bitten they'll like you.
Well-balanced progressive gamplay that keeps you from becoming too powerful, whilst hard work/dedication/planning pay off greatly
Cons:
40 hours in and I'm yet to find something bad about the game that wasn't caused by oversight or just plain stupidity on my part

Pros:

Cons:

It's not a particularly good port and most reviews seem to emphasise that so I'm not going to bother going into that side of things. Instead I'll just focus on the game itself, which I was able to play without any issue through to the end and then some.
The game is fantastic. It's on-par with Dishonored 1 in terms of pretty much every gameplay aspect. The ability to choose two different characters is a nice little feature, though I always felt the story makes more sense if you play Corvo instead of Emily (which is unusual, since in the opening few minutes you do play as Emily; including in the optional tutorial).
It has equally interesting characters, encounters and levels. The levels are slightly larger, though I wouldn't say they're massively more open that Dishonored 1's levels. Still, they are bigger and there seems to be more attention to detail in them.
Enemy AI is smarter. They will notice if you leave a door open, if someone goes missing from their patrol route and if on any stage of alert except the basic "nothing's happening", they will spot you quite easily if you're in any way in their line of site.
It goes without saying that "killing everything" is still the easier route to go down, but this time they've added non-lethal combat and more variety of non-lethal takedowns to make non-lethal a little bit easier. Interestingly Sleep Darts seem a lot harder to come by, though perhaps I wasn't exploring the right places.
The story is about as good as Dishonored 1's was, but the voice acting of the player protagonist definitely helps add to character. While I was nervous about Corvo being voiced as opposed to being silent as he was in the first game, I was surprised to find out that Corvo is voiced by the same actor as Garrett from the first few Thief games and it fits him absolutely perfectly. Additionally, the way he speaks, reacts to things and thinks to himself really add to the character because the writing really seems to nail down who Corvo is in the current stage of his life. Another nice touch is how you can definitely tell he is an older and more veteran Corvo and how he almost feels to be a successor to Daud from the first game.
The Outsider's voice was a mild disappointment, since Billy Lush wasn't asked to return to Dishonored 2 to voice him. While still a fantastic performance, the new Outsider seems more hyperactive than the old one. He moves around, he speaks far more than he used to and he seems a little like he's on a low dose of cocaine; whereas Dishonored 1's Outsider was clearly absolutely impartial to everything, slower in tone and actions and only spoke enough to leave the player in wonder.
Other than that, the atmosphere, the music, the improved graphics, the level-design and side-quests all make Dishonored 2 a worthy successor to the first game. It's not better, but it's as good as.

I really want to recommend this game. I really do. I waited in line for the oringinal Dishonored for the 360, played it for countless hours. I've bought it on Steam, played it through again, then bought the DLC and played as [Secondary Character] because I love both the game, and the world, so much.
Don't get me wrong, the story world in Dishonored 2 is very much enjoyable. There's lore aplenty if you read through the countless books, leaflets, and newspapers you pick up. Plus, the artstyle is very much the same. The colors are intense, and not much is lacking for detail.
However, this is the part that I don't like.
My rig is very much able to run at "Ultra". However, whenever [my character] is able to look into the distance, which can be quite vast, it feels as though I need to wear glasses because suddenly my 20/20 vision is for naught. Everything, even the objects in close view, look very fuzzy. Almost as though I've stepped into the light of day for the first time and my eyes need time to adjust.
Not only that, but occasionally the screen lags for countless seconds. Jump out of one window into a new area and suddenly I need to wait at least 30-45 seconds for the game to be responsive again. Luckily, I've not encountered an enemy in that time. I know that if I did, [my character] would be dead. Or severely injured at the very least.
As I said, I very much want to give this game the thumbs up, because I like the original and its DLC so much, but until preformance issues can be dealt with, I fear that I cannot.

All in all I'd recommend this game to anyone that likes creative PvP games. 8/10.

It's a perfect re-release of The First and Second Encounter (and expansions) of the Serious Sam franchise (I prefer to forget BFE).  Now, it's got slightly improved textures and widescreen support-- but keep in mind, this project is very new, and needs to get a foothold on bugs and such before they get down to fixing the graphics and all.  It is labeled "Early Access..."
If you don't know what Serious Sam is...
1) What the hell were you doing 10 years ago, back when we could actually play console games and not be overly disappointed with bugs?
2) Know that just by looking at the name on the Steam store page, you should have already purchased this.  Well, if you didn't trust it after BFE, your reluctance is at least understandable...
It's pretty much, to describe it as blandly as I can, a first person Rambo-style (as in the real Rambo, not that movie-game crap) where you fight aliens and re-animated soldiers like a badass.  It's kind of like Duke Nukem, but less cheap call ladies and more giant one eyed things that need professional facial displacement services.
If you've ever liked Serious Sam, get this game immediately.  It's the classics, sure, not exactly super-HDX-ultrapower-graphicalness, but it's still good enough nonetheless.  It's got full multiplayer support carried over, and it's a lot more compatible with modern systems.  It does a great job of optimizing itself so that you don't have to, though you're welcome to go through its options whenever you feel like it.
It has full workshop support with downloads permitted, custom map support, and mutators.  Jack up that enemy count to 600% and start pulling that trigger... you may or may not like its effect on Kamikaze units.
Even in an early access state, this game is awesome.  It's also a great starting point in the series, since it comes with both the First and Second encounter, and maybe the second game entirely.  I'm not sure.
This puts away the mess we saw with BFE, and I'm ready for another Serious Sam title.  As long as hitscan-wielding enemies are as rare as they are in this game, we'll be set.

This review was written just after the 'excavation' update was shipped.
Astroneer has undergone several considerable update over the past few months that deepen and revitalize its replay value. Early iterations produced an experience that was good for 6-10 hours of game play before its novelty wore off, though starting a new save file and exploring a new procedurally-generated world means replay value is high for a game that is still undergoing mechanical innovation.
One frustration/amusement for me is how older save files gradually become unplayable as updates are rolled put - changes in gravity cause vehicles and found objects to float into the air or sink through the ground, and ground tiles begin to desync along their edges, like strips of paper being pulled away that you can stand on and see under. This makes it difficult to continue to use saves that significant time has been invested into.
The game is foundationally sound, with few process interruptions, and existing bugs aren't game-breaking. Astroneer doesn't punish new players in their first few playthroughs (though experienced players will probably run through a few save files before finding a favorable spawn that enables faster research, base development and resource collection). Recent mechanical changes suggest that the learning curve of the game will increase as certain features (particularly the deform tool) become more complex to use.

I have only played a small anount at the time of writing this, but I believe I have made some sound judgments on the game.
It is an MMORPG. This may come as to shock to some that don't pay attention to the store page, website, and game description, but yes it is not like the other Elder Scrolls series in that regard. Yes you do have to Pay to Play (for now) so a valid payment method will be needed to get started even with the free 30 days you get on purchase. I have played other MMORPGs and I know how these games work so I was not surprised, but I see a lot of people are getting frustrated at this fact and making  many negative reviews because of it. Your opinion about subcripions aside, the way the game makes the money it needs to survive is not a negative or a positive just because you don't look before you leap.
With that out of the way, ESO is in my opinion a very fun MMORPG. It has a few problems with immersion as compared with the single player Elder Scrolls games and I will admit that it isn't as rewarding to complete the minor quests due to the copy and paste cast of minor characters, but it is a MMO symptom of the level grind in early stages. There is a problem with how you play with friends as well which does hamper what is the most potentially fun about the game, of course I do believe these things will be fixed shortly as the game is early in its life. My biggest complaint is also something I expected is the missing expectation to be a one man (or lady) death incarnate, losing that epic feel of really being the chosen one does take away from an Elder Scrolls experience.
As I said I think ESO is very fun and if some of the minor problems get patched and we get the content that we are being promised I do believe it will become my favorite MMORPG to date. As far as favorite in the franchise Morrowind still holds that title and I doubt that it will get dethroned any time soon (although Skyrim came close and I will always have a special place for Arena on my shelf). I am still very excited to see the parts of Tamriel that I have not seen since the earlier installments and explore lore and fiction that will most likely be added to a new single player installment of the Elder Scrolls series. IF you are an Elder Scrolls fan and an MMO fan this game is right for you now. IF you just want to play the game to keep up with the world of Tamriel I would recommend waiting until it goes free to play (as any MMO in todays market will and should).
ESO gets a 6/10 at the moment from me. mainly because I do not always play with others and soloing can be difficult at times, but take that with a grain of salt as the game gets patched it will get better and as I get further up in level my opinion my change.

SO after having a very negative review of this game over a year ago, i have returned and fell in love. it has been improved on every level and to be honest should have been released this year in retrospect ... totally worth a buy now if you are a fan of ES and MMOs.

What is there to say about Dark Souls 2... I woud recommend it to anyone who loves Melee combat games and RPG's where you are not hand holded. I played it on the XBOX 360 and beat it... but my 360 died the next day.
So I purchased the PC version and it is so much better than the Console versions.  Looks good, smooth gameplay, and the multiplayer connection problems were a ton better than the 360 version.  After 60 hours in the PC version - I beat it three times and got 100% Acheivements.
If you have never played Dark Souls or Demon Souls.  Dark Soulss 2 is a third person view fantasy world/combat game that allows for precise melee combat and range magic/bows.  The combat can be awkward but rewarding once you figure it out.  It has RPG Elements of stat points as you level and armor/weapons to collect and enhance their strength.
The multiplayer is unlike any other game series.  People can invade your single player game to try and kill you... or you can summon them for a level/boss fight - but they disappear back to their world after the fight.  If you kill a bunch of good guy NPC's, then people can invade your world to kill you as revenge.  There is also areas for PVP that allow a que up process or hang out in an area to be attacked/invaded.
This game has a ton of bosses - 20+ and a lot of different areas to explore.  The First play through will likely take 30-40 hours but the second play through will take about 10-15 because you get to keep all your gear/levels.  By my third play through I did it under 7 or 8 hours.
Technically the game is still quite hard if you never played a "Souls", but not as hard as Dark Souls 1.  That is only because I find that Dark Souls 2 is more fair than Dark Souls 1 because part one had a lot of spots that were cheap deaths or the poor direction.  Dark Souls 2 fixed these so it is more accessible for people who hate games that kill hem over and over, but you'll still die a lot in this game because they increased the combat difficulty for normal monsters by increasing the volume of them and bosses.
Not as rewarding as other souls games when you beat a tough boss, but still a great game and better made than the previous two technically but not as easily adored as the previous two souls games.
Totally worth it and an awesome game.  If you watch a video and the combat looks fun or you want a good RPG game with responsive/precise combat where your skills = in game skills - then buy it and play it.  You'll yell at it and get angry, but you'll want to continue to play!
Where's the fun in struggling with the control system and dying every 5 seconds?  AVOID!

It really looked promising and the game was fun at the start, until all the bugs kicked in and turned it into an unfinishable mess.
It's so buggy, that I can't even finish the game. Even after an update that "added map markers to the regional threats mission" - I see no arrows for that mission and I'm at war with 3 different factions.

The game has all the content to be a great survival game - scavenging, base constructing, farming, item crafting, diplomacy, trading... unfortunately it suffers from a terrible lack of balance that completely breaks realism.
First, the zombies aren't actually 'fast zombies', they are 'olympic runner zombies'. They will charge you from beyond your seeing distance at the speed of a cheetah and then lunge at you from 3 meters away to tackle you. Combat is just 'dodge - shoot - dodge - shoot' until your enemies are dead. There's no room for strategy/tactics or even a little bit of thinking. It isn't difficult, but it lacks depth and quickly becomes uninteresting. And in case you're wondering, there's no stealth mechanic so zombies always aggro you before you can see them, no way around this.
The shooting mechanics are also frustrating - guns are very inaccurate even at close range. The characters could miss the side of a barn at 10 feet, literally. And since zombies have quite a bit of health, you'll empty a few clips to kill them. If you wait without moving long enough, you can make a perfectly accurate shot but this rarely happens since you're fighting marathon runner zombies. The time it takes to aim a perfect shot at 3 feet is way too long anyway to be realistic.
Then there's ammo - there's too much of it lying around to be realistic or to feel like you're struggling to scavenge for supplies. Out of bullets? Just search the nearest house or car and I guarantee you'll find enough to kill a few zombies. Yes, since guns are so inaccurate it's a good thing there's lots of ammo, but why not just make guns more accurate and give the player less ammo? At least it would feel realistic and like you're actually in a post-apocalyptic world were supplies are scarce. Right now it feels like the entire US Air Force airdropped all their ammo reserves over the game map.
Next problem is the inventory size. Characters can't carry a lot of stuff without backpacks so scavenging runs are very unproductive. The ammo you need to carry with you also takes up a lot of inventory room even if you just carry enough at once to kill 5 zombies. This isn't a problem when you have backpacks, but it can take time to find them. And by the way, you NEED a backpack if you want a character to do any construction. Construction requires you to carry a heavy toolbox + construction materials, you can't just drop the materials at the construction site and then come back with the tools to complete the job. Without a backpack, most characters don't have enough inventory room to build anything. That means when you leave someone at base to build stuff, that's one less backpack you can give your guys going out to find supplies. It also means the first backpack you find won't help you scavenge because building barricades will be more important at that point, so you'll have to keep looking for another one if you want your scavenging runs to actually become productive.
Then there's the time lapse. The days just go by too fast. Your characters have to regularly eat, drink, sleep and some have medical conditions that require taking meds like diabetes/insulin. So whenever I speak to an NPC, I feel like I'm wasting precious time. Seriously, a 2 minute conversation feels like a terrible, unproductive waste of time. I never ask NPCs about their backstory, I only use dialogue for quests or trading. And when I speak to an NPC, I just quickly fly over the dialogue.
And with time flying by so fast, well you need to get food and meds quickly. Your characters will eat them up almost faster than you can get them, especially the meds. Just like with combat, there's no time to think or plan, you have to keep moving.
This isn't a survival game, it's a fast-paced arcade game with survival elements. And it's a shame, because it could be an awesome survival game just by modifying a few variables.
Sure, it's only five bucks. But then again, it's a game I quickly gave up playing with no intention of playing it again. It's a game I want to enjoy, but it needs modifications to be an actual survival game and less of an arcade game. Right now it feels like the devs just had no idea how to balance difficulty properly in a game, so they made zombies sprint, they made your guns less accurate than a nerf gun, and then they gave you thousands of ammo lying around everywhere to make sure you wouldn't run out.
Would sure be nice if they fixed this or at least provided a minimum of mod support. It's just stupid how close this came to being a really great game in it's genre, yet failed completely.

So far I am not convinced by Dishonored 2. I liked the original Dishonored because I thought that the levels were well thought out, there was a sufficient amount of enemies per area so that one might be challenged yet still have fun. Here, it appears that enemy guards are more or less everywhere, and it is nigh impossible to go through an area undetected.
Do not get me wrong, I like sneaking games and I like the challenge of being able to sneak by guards to get to my goal.  What is the point of playing a sneaking game if there is zero challenge, right? However, I would argue that in Dishonored 2, as soon as you get spotted, you immediately get a plethora of guards who rush and swarm you seemingly out of nowhere.
I will perhaps change my mind as I keep playing through the levels (bear in mind that I am only at the second location in the game), as they might get better.
For now, this is an entirely subjective opinion based on very little game time, and is subject to change. I sure hope so, anyway.
-EDIT-
So after playing some more I have decided to wait until the patch. My main issue here, as it should be stated, has nothing to do with performance. I am one of the lucky few who has no real FPS drop. I have the occasional drop to 45-50, but nothing groundbreaking. I also have a couple of lighting issues and pathfinding bugs for the enemy guards, which is annoying but not really my big issue.
My big issue relies upon the fact that enemy guards always seem to know where you are hiding. Or they will suddenly get alerted of your presence despite you being behind a wall or on another floor (which will arguably be updated during the patch, hence my waiting). Also, civilians for no apparent reason will run away from you and call the guards, shouting "I DON'T WANT TO DIE LIKE THIS!!" despite the player having done absolutely nothing.
So long story short, I'll give the game another go around, once they are done patching it. So far, I'd hold off if I were you.

Probably the best PC RPG ever made. We completely owe the existance of every Fallout game and any dystopian RPG made after it. The game is a masterpiece and truly mindblowing to think that a game of this scale and depth was made in 1988, when computer could just about manage your basic text editor and 64 colour graphics. It might look and play absolutely terribly by todays standards, not letting you see your battles or encounters ther than a few onscreen messages and looking completely like a game of it's era, with very hefty pixels and almost laughable character design, but, the game is one of it's kind, offering something that was unheard of in 1988, an RPG, that was set on earth, with humans, in a dystopian futuristic wasteland of a 21st century gone bad. This game was basically the precurssor to the first 2 Fallout games, and it shows, in terms of overall design and gameplay, they're nearly identical, albeit, a bit more pixelated. It's really the kinda game you damn well need to look for the PDF of the manual that comes with the game, find the nearest printer, and print off into a small book and find the nearest walkthrough, or else you're going to be in for a bad time. It's almost impossible to understand just what the hell is going on. Wasteland is also probably the hardest game on Steam (yes, the entirety of Steam, I've never come across a game so frustratingly difficult, almost insulting at times as it's possible to get killed amost as soon as you enter a new area), but aside from that, Wasteland is a great game and is by far the best game of the 1980's. It really is one of the few games (the others being XCOM/UFO and in FPS terms, DOOM) that took games into places never thought possible, replacing tired, arcade mechanics with rich, deep storylines and immersive gameplay. It's the kind of game that you have to be in a 1988 mindset to even play, as I'm sure the majority of people will buy it on a Steam sale and play it for 30 minutes before abandoning it, but that would be doing it an injustice. Pick up this game, it's a masterpiece, albiet, a 1988 masterpiece.

This game has aged very poorly, but not like most games. The (non-remastered) graphics, sound, and interface all held up fairly well, though they definitely feel old-school. There's a certain charm that comes with that. No, the problem lies with the mechanics.
There are a lot things in this game that game developers have since learned are Bad Ideas and we
. Things like rolling character stats, dead stats, no descriptions of skills except in a separate manual that the steam version doesn't come with, obscure combat rules, no item/weapon descriptions or stats, manually using skills like 'perception' - and this is all just what I encountered in the first ten minutes.
It might not be fair to judge a 1988 game by 2016 standards, but I can't do it any other way. I'm not interested in being an impartial judge of what is or was contemporaneously a good game. I'm interested in telling you whether or not a game is worth buying and playing. Wasteland 1 is not fun to play and I do not recommend it.

I've spent hundreds of hours in this game before it was available on Steam.
Smite is a MOBA like DotA or League of Legends in which 2 teams of 5 players fight on a map to achive certain objectives based on the map type. What sets this apart from other MOBAs is:
- The unique third person view point, this alone makes it a very compelling experience compared to classic MOBAs.  What comes with this is that every shot, even basic attacks are skill shots and being situationally aware is a much different experience if you can't see behind yourself.
- Instead of random made up heroes, you play gods from various cultures around the worth
- There are several game play modes; Conquest (classic MOBA 3 lane map), Joust (3v3 with 1 main lane and 2 jungle lanes), Arena (5v5 deathmatch), Assault (1 lane all random), Siege (4v4 2 lane 1 jungle lane). There is also a Match of the Day which rotates every day, these are fun/crazy tweaks to the other game modes such as reducing mana costs, cooldowns or forcing a handfull of gods.
- An in game voice system that uses keystrokes allows smooth play and communication between players of different languages. For example VRR = Retreat!, VAT1 = Attack left tower, etc.
It's worth noting that this game is free to play with no pay to win aspects. Hirez Games monetizes the game using primarily god skins and a one time package to buy all the gods. The god package also refunds any "favor" spent to unlock gods beforehand, so it becomes better value the longer you play.

UPDATE: They've fixed Crossfire and it is now supported mostly through the Steam version of Smite.
There are still and will most likely forever be intermitent ping issues.
But now that they've made the game playable, I would recommend this to anyone that enjoys MOBAs, or MMOs, or just anyone that likes a fun game. The playstyle is like a mixture of World of Warcraft and DOTA-likes. There is a massive pool of gods(heroes), which some are apparently modeled after the DOTA-like hero models, but there is a lot of originality in most of the character design. There are multiple fun modes and a Match of The Day feature. Match of the day is a random, often user/designer submited, version of their map pool mixed with different god restrictions/cool down reduction/gold spooling etc..
There is definitely a lot of fun to be had and hours of replayability in this game.

Ok so this review will be based on my 2.5 year experience with APB.
Basically it's a cops vs criminals open world game where 2 sides are facing each other during missions (you basically ready up while beind in the "out of mission mode" and you are being put in a mission with other random teammates or your premade group against some people from the opposite faction). You have a really wide selection of weapons and vehicles. You can even apply modifications to your character, weapons and vehicles. The game itself is great and the gameplay is really enjoyable after you become decent at the game. It contains lots of customization, you can change your character's appearance, you can create symbols and put them or your clothes or even on your body as tattoos, you can also design cars and get weapon skins, you can even compose your own songs and create death themes (people hear them when you kill them ;)). So basically you can customize to your heart's content. Overall one of the best games I've played so far and I will even risk saying that if APB was managed properly it could be as famous as CS:GO.
But then as a decent player let me tell you about the dark side of this game because I think that's what matters the most. The game is managed by a terrible company who is focusing only on getting sales on the in-game ARMAS Marketplace (yes you need to pay real money) the company promised us many many great features like improved match making or chat filtering or even the upgrade of a really outdated game engine. Years have passed and nothing has been done but yet new items on the marketplace such as clothing packs and usually overpowered broken weapons (which are of course being nerfed after the sales are dropping) are still appearing. Another really sad thing about this game is cheating. Yes the company added an anti-cheat called FairFight which was used in some other games as well and it was kind of working at the beginning but now the cheaters are going wild again. Some people still doubt if this anti-cheat really got implemented because of how poorly it works. This is a really competitive game so you need to spend years in it to be able to take down the top players and most of it depends on your dedication, skill and of course your gear, just like it is in CS:GO. While in CS:GO all that matters is your accuracy, ability to control the weapon and good awareness in APB accuracy and staying on the target at all times matters the most, there's no such thing as headshots or anything (one big hitbox) and people have more health than in CS:GO. People move really fast, they dodge to the sides, they camp the corners (you just need to overcome their chaotic movement and stay on the target). Back to the topic because the cheating is really really bad right now people tend to hackusate each other and that especially happens when you are a decent player (you will be getting tons of hackusations, you will be called names but it's kind of a good thing if that happens because you will know that you are improving and even though you are a legit player, other people are considering you a cheater) another bad part about cheating is that the game is free so even though someone gets banned, that person can just create a new account and keep playing. The game is basically full of toxic people, internet gangsters and kids but there are some nice people too. So now I should summarize. Really one of the best games I ever played, really solid mechanics, lots of customization and a really enjoyable gameplay (the con is that you need to spend an insane amount of time in it to become decent and be able to play on a decent level, most new players usually leave when they are getting stomped by old players but hey there are districts for players with lower skill level too, but even there you can encounter some smurfs from time to time),  the game is owned by a really greedy company that very very very rarely keeps it's promises and mainly focuses on getting more money. The last thing is a toxic unforgiving community which will ruin your mood within minutes if not seconds but if you are up to the task and you are not afraid to accept the challenge and sign the pact then its definitely a game for you ! ;) If you will dedicate lots of time to it and you will keep playing for months or years you will become decent at it and salty people won't be scary anymore ;)

Let me start off by saying I am enjoying this game and this is going to be a positive review. That being said I think that I  understand where some of the bad reviews are coming from. If you are a player who enjoys rushing to cap by planning the most efficient quest paths, min maxing your character just so, and skipping every bit of dialouge along the way. This game will immediately be a let down for you. In fact you'll probably be miserable most of the time while in-game.
So my first weekend here with many hours logged only saw my character hit level 12, and still has only seen my starting zone and island (khajiit) thus far..... BUT I've been exploring all of the map markers, figuring out any puzzles, knocking out any side quests I happen to wander into, trying to reach all of the shards, harvesting crafting mats, fishing, tinkering with the crafting options, and basically fiddling about at my own pace.
As someone who used to take pride in running up a new max level toon as quickly as was possible and then diving into raids/end-game, that's a bit of a departure for me. But As a long time Elder Scrolls fan (all the way back to arena) I wanted to give this game an honest go despite the bad press. Since I've already seen and heard the thoughts of others on this, I went into this game knowing that it would not fit into my usual play style. Knowing that up front has allowed me to slow down and enjoy the game for what it is rather than try to make it something it is not.
Is it a great social game, meh, not that I've seen so far although the community seems decent enough. Are the group mechanics great, not sure haven't tried them. Has it got the bomb diggity end game? No idea, I'll cross that bridge when I get there. Is the PVP hot sauce? Not sure, to be honest I've been too busy fiddling about with all of the other content. Is it $15/month, yes, and I'm okay with that..... seriously, it's $15, that's 3.5 gallons of gas (at the moment), a night of delivery pizza, a case of cheap beer, or a movie with popcorn and a drink if you're not paying for a date. I'm Pretty sure if you're that hard up for $15 on a monthly basis you should look into cheaper hobbies..... but I digress.
If you go into this game with the proper expectations, and if you're willing to read/listen to the quest content, read some of the books and stuff you find laying around, take time to craft and explore, and most importantly enjoy the trip to cap as much if not more than being there, then, and only then, would I recommend this whole heartedly.

Bob have maneged to single-handedly create a game that surpass most industry titles in gameplay, story and even character building. And, I am already looking forward to the next playthrough, with some different choices. Works wonders as a sandbox game too.

ALMOST the ultimate zombie survival game!
You follow a hedge fund manager who took the ultimate hedge: he stocked an emergency bunker in the Mojave desert in case of a disaster.  And it paid off.
Manage multiple settlement members, press-gang thugs and looters to join you, keep your populace happy, keep everyone fed (or they'll get stupid), watch out for the undead trailing you back to your base, and looters tracking you back as well.
Social and reputation mechanics are simple but functional, though they could be a bit more transparent.  Transportation and water are your most important concerns.  Different grades of infected and infection serve different levels of danger.
The ONLY reason this game isn't THE BEST is that it lacks a bit of 'full feature' fleshing out.
I'd like to see:
more structures (kitchen/canteen, concrete barricades, mine, tents, barbed wire, stakes, irrigation...)
more types of food (particularly involving nutrition and craft cooking!  We can't eat corn forever!)
more crafting (melee weapons, fletching, clothes, duct-tape engineering)
more advancement (wooden fences have an upgrade, mines add rails, people start asking for hot showers and solar heaters)
vehicles and gasoline scavenging
house dangers (narrow sightlines and darkness make buildings more dangerous than being outside in the daytime!)
Annexing buildings (I know 'the dead can smell where we used to live', but surely they can smell where twenty people are living NOW, too!  Don't just let us, MAKE us claim certain kinds of pre-disaster buildings for benefits and requirements!)
And of course...  character creation.  I'd really like to start a sandbox style of game with all of this going on that doesn't force me to play the jackass hedge fund manager.  Don't get me wrong, I LOVE that the hedgefund manager is a jackass, not a negotiator, but the interplay between social skills, potential, and current skill level makes for some intriguing characters, not to mention the little things like lung cancer, or being a diabetic (which the game ALREADY HAS!).

For those who are new - Dishonored 2 is a stealth action game with some magic that you can choose to take or refuse it and play with only your trusty sword and crossbow. Dishonored 2 is set in an industrialization age filled with poverty and corruption where you must re-take the crown you lost by eliminating your enemies. How you do that is up to you and that is what makes this game great.
Re-playability - I don’t think this game has that much re-playability because once you have completed the game you have a sense of what path to take next time when you decide to do your low or high chaos run. Sure you could take the left path instead of the right path like you did in your first run but the end result is the same one of the paths was just easier to take.
Length of the game – That all depends on your play style and how good you are at stealth games. For me when I tried to do a low chaos run which means not killing anyone and trying to not get spotted took me about 12 hours to finish the game.
Not working for everyone - About the frame issues I don’t know what everyone is talking about I was able to play the game on high settings and stream it for a friend with no frame loss. There are a couple of small areas in the game where I did feel the frames drop but I only experienced it three or four times. If it helps I am using a GeForce GTX 750 Ti.
Complaints – Each mission feels the same with some differences but I feel like they has some really cool ideas but they did not use them enough. The last thing I want is possibly a new game+.
If you can’t play this game right now then I hope you will be able to once they fix the issues you are having because it is an amazing game worth playing. If you are hesitant about picking up the game because you don’t know if your computer will run well with it and you don’t have deep pockets you can always wait for it to be fixed or pick it up and give it a shot steam has a refund button if it does not work out for you.

I highly recommend this game if you like a challenge. For those who get easily discouraged when you die and lose varying degrees of progress, this game isn't for you. This game is all about dying  (or rather, trying not to), as you will do a lot of it.
First off, the graphics of this game are much better than its predesessor Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition. However, I cannot say if the controls setup is better (as the first game's was atroscious) as I use a controller.
Without any spoilers I will say that this game has a lot more bosses than the first game, adding more challenge and more suspense to every fog door that you encounter. So far I have greatly enjoyed almost all of the boss battles that I have run across. And, while I have beaten some areas, I did go back to explore segments that I missed previously only to be surprised at a boss battle that I had circled around and avoided the first time.
At the start of the game (after the prologue) you are given the ability to fast travel immediately, which I find to be a boon when I need to backtrack to an area that I think (or would like to) is safe. Especially since the game will start back up from wherever you quit from, not spawning you back at your last bonfire.
There is a higher challenge with this game, however, as enemies will stop spawning after you have either killed them or have been killed in the area 15 times. An item may be used to respawn enemies, but they will be at a higher difficulty and this is a permanent game changing effect (as when you beat the game and go to NG+ the area will then be considered NG++) which also effects all bosses in that specific area. This can be annoying at early levels when souls are needed to get better equipment or for levelling up and you have to travel to more difficult areas to gain souls.
All in all this game is fun, agrivating, addicting, infuriating and all around a must have to any gamer who loves a challenge. Go buy it already!
Oh If you use a controller, check the controls and turn auto run off at the beginning of the game. You'll waste less stamina that way. <3

So far I am not convinced by Dishonored 2. I liked the original Dishonored because I thought that the levels were well thought out, there was a sufficient amount of enemies per area so that one might be challenged yet still have fun. Here, it appears that enemy guards are more or less everywhere, and it is nigh impossible to go through an area undetected.
Do not get me wrong, I like sneaking games and I like the challenge of being able to sneak by guards to get to my goal.  What is the point of playing a sneaking game if there is zero challenge, right? However, I would argue that in Dishonored 2, as soon as you get spotted, you immediately get a plethora of guards who rush and swarm you seemingly out of nowhere.
I will perhaps change my mind as I keep playing through the levels (bear in mind that I am only at the second location in the game), as they might get better.
For now, this is an entirely subjective opinion based on very little game time, and is subject to change. I sure hope so, anyway.
-EDIT-
So after playing some more I have decided to wait until the patch. My main issue here, as it should be stated, has nothing to do with performance. I am one of the lucky few who has no real FPS drop. I have the occasional drop to 45-50, but nothing groundbreaking. I also have a couple of lighting issues and pathfinding bugs for the enemy guards, which is annoying but not really my big issue.
My big issue relies upon the fact that enemy guards always seem to know where you are hiding. Or they will suddenly get alerted of your presence despite you being behind a wall or on another floor (which will arguably be updated during the patch, hence my waiting). Also, civilians for no apparent reason will run away from you and call the guards, shouting "I DON'T WANT TO DIE LIKE THIS!!" despite the player having done absolutely nothing.
So long story short, I'll give the game another go around, once they are done patching it. So far, I'd hold off if I were you.

Catharsis personified.
In short, Slime Rancher is a farm simulator game that revolves around caring for and carroling adorable little slimes. And battling them when they get out of hand. You feed them various vegetables or chickens to get resources out of them that you sell for money. This money then allows you to upgrade your gear and infrastructure so that you can do the previous tasks better. The cycle repeats ad naseum until you hit the current end of development like a brick wall.
It is a simple game, but a glorious one. The questionable moral implications of how you care for these creatures coupled with their adorable demeanor and the various ways that they can kill you, explosive radiation and crystal shards in my case, makes for a delightful package. Did the raw mechanics wow me? No. Did the experience soothe me in a way that only copious drugs could do? Yes. A very tearful and happy yes.

Honestly I'm not going to dump on this game because it's not a bad game, it's not trying to be Skyrim Online at all, it's trying to be it's own online experience set in the Elder Scrolls universe. Now before you go ahead and give me hell because you're a huge fan of the ES then wait and let me explain, take into account that this isn't trying to be a successor to one of the greatest rpgs of the last generation, and read this review to the fullest.
This game is pure MMO fun, it has all of the basic necessities that an MMO needs to stay afloat, but it's not the epic Skyrim sequel fans were waiting for. This game is huge, the open world spans across the entirety of Tamriel and has many factions, races, and classes that are all capable of commiting to either roll in the holy trinity. This game has some of the best systems whether it's crafting, combat, or social, it's all nicely balanced and is all locked in to make up one of the best in the genre. The pvp and dungeons are where it's at for this game, while you get the entire province of Cyrodil to battle in, your goals are to capture strongholds and take full control of the map, now that's well designed pvp. Also questing is done fairly well in this game but can become a bit grindy, but with any MMO, that is to be expected.
You should always be playing with friends and groups which are another one of the games features that are handled really well. You can easily set up a small questing group, a dungeon group, or a raid with just a quick group finder feature that set's you up with other people that are interested in grouping for either activity.
Now I know that there are some that just won't let this game have a break because it isn't Skyrim, but from what I just told you, I think you should play atleast 20+ hours before you pass total judgement and cross it off your list, because it's not an ES game, but it is a great MMO and a great time.

Fantastic.  I could not have been much happier with the modifications made in this game compared to the original(in terms of raw gameplay, I missed out on PC issues in the original as I played it through a console).  Tuning things, like equipment degredation rate up, but allowing for it to be regenerated by resting at a bonfire is a remarkable way to force the player to cause the inhabitants that have been trogged through to respawn more fequently.  The challenge is still here, and of course they have the oppurtunity for you the player to make life more miserable if you're a masochist by starting out barren and with no hope at leveling up except by forcing foes off cliffs.  Lastly involving gameplay, framerate is everything.  This game actually seems to manage its resources more dynamically allowing for steady and fast framerate through most of the game, but even allowing for settings to be altered to best accomodate your experience with your PC build(sadly a "feature" considering the port of the first was apparently lacking this).  Playing the first game on a console with an inconsistent frame rate forced me to have to play by way of anticipation, with control input tied to the framerate learning to be successful was painful.  With the faster input response to smoother gameplay, my mistakes feel truly like they are my fault entirely in this game.
Aside from general gameplay I would like to mention the graphics.  It was a shock seeing the gameplay looking very different from a playable build demonstrated last year, but it is not as if the game is lacking in stunning visuals.  If you played through the first game you would have noticed some variety with the environments in their presentation.  Overall everything was low in raw geometry but had intriguing textures.  And most of the games graphical details came from false geometry shown in many different ways through the textures(normal maps, bump mapping, etc..).  While texture to geometry effects are still highly used to detail the world there is more geometry overall when compared to the first game, even if it wasn't there these high resolution textures(and texture effects) look incredible and I am certain the game would still have a powerful visual aesthetic.  Aside from that they do have pretty lighting and particle effects.  Game looks nice, end of that story.
I thought I could summarize everything in those two briefings: of gameplay and graphics, but still I linger on to all I enjoy in this game and I could easily trail off for a decent amount of time describing it.  For the sake of me shutting up to play some more I will add that the multiplayer experience feels much better to me.  I never went hardcore in PvP in the first game, and I don't see myself doing so for awhile in the second(if at all) but the community at large feels more alive while playing the sequel.  Message markers are everywhere fooling people or genuinely offering tips(for some reason everyone wants to lie about illusory walls, or warn about falling in holes yet people still run down them) and the rating system seems to be more responsive now(a side note is now you don't use a "soap stone" to write messages, there is a message tab on the start menu).  Blood pools are everywhere, allowing you to laugh at horribly bad mistakes or to inspect where traps or ambushes might occur by watching the spectral figure dying in front of you.  I have also found the invading system is improved, by which I mean I like it more in the sequel.  I don't want to get into more details then that as it would spoil discovery and such, but basically this is a single player game made dynamic by involving other people playing it at the same time.  While being invaded in the first game kept things interesting it really impeded on my opportuniy to discover new things, and though it did completely offer that hardcore experience it brought more anger than fun.  But now knowing when I am going to be experiencing a fight(and they get horribly fun and engaging) and when I know I will need to summon for help then giving back and helping someone else through a challenge feels much more rewarding then it ever did in the first game.  Oh by the by though, I am getting eager to play so I will end this by also mentioning there is a memorial that gives a live global death count, last I looked something like 51,000,000+ deaths.
