I may come back and modify this review after a while, but here goes.
APB: Reloaded is about the closest thing I've found to "GTA Online f2p" (not that I was looking very hard, mind you). You got your criminals, and your police foce (known formally as "Enforcers") duking it out in mission based combat in 1 of 2 rather large cities.
You got your "Financial" District, a large map with lots of buildings that offers close to mid range combat.
The "Waterfront" District, another large map with slightly less buildings that offers more mid to far range combat.
Instead of writing a paragraph of my experiences and such, I'm just gonna go with a good ol pros and cons list.
Pros:
+Relatively large setting
+Ok graphics
+Solid TPS gameplay (because this IS a third person shooter)
+Funny community
+More *confirmed* girls in this game than any other game I've played (instert a good lenny face here)
+Good customization options
+Cars
+Not necessarily p2w
There's probably more, but I'm writing this review at 8AM, so I'm probably forgetting stuff.
Here's somma dem cons
Cons:
- Somewhat poor weapon choice (It seems that there's about 2-3 weapons per role (smg, shotty, assault rifles, etc.) and most of it is just variations of weapons with mods and stuff, or they look slightly different)
-Server lag happens sometimes
-That funny community can be a bad one at times
-It looks p2w (I mean, I can drop bodies pretty well with a paid weapon, I have and I currently do; but I dropped quite a few bodies with the beginner weap or the slow shooting uzi thing. You can do good without paying imo)
-Relatively small community
-Eventually, the missions get repetitive. It's usually, go here, break into this thing, steal the other thing, now kill each other 12 times (or worse, those dreaded VIP missions ughh)
-BS happens sometimes (SOMETIMES THESE PEOPLE JUST WONT DIE!)
-Hackers happen (but a ton of people get banned daily, so, yay?)
-Silver districts are filled with golds, which makes things hard (as they've established themselves for a while probably), so most stilvers play on bronze districts, which might make it suck for new bronze players, contributing to that "this game is so p2w" feeling. I too am guilty of this (because despite me hours logged into this game, I'm still a little more than a week or two old in this game. Still noob ;w; )
And probably more stuff than 8AM me can think of right now.
Would I recommend this game? Kinda. I'd warn you going in, though, that it's gonna be ragey sometimes, but I think you might be able to have some fun.
-Sincerely, SethRussel/DragonPope

TL;DR Serious Sam Revolution is a must have for any TRUE serious sam fan.

Ahhh, Serious Sam...a budget-priced, nostalgic bundle of fun to many. And well...that counts to me; somewhat. I mean, the first SS game I played was Next Encounter for the PS2, and it was a crazy good time! But what about the classic games? Despite their large fan community and mod support; something didn't feel quite..."modern" with the games.
Enter Serious Sam Revolution, a fan-made version of the classic Serious Sam titles made by some of the most well-known and diehard SS fans from around the globe. While it's in Early Access at the moment, the full version of Revolution will include a new campaign, new gamemodes and much more. And how did this grab my attention? Well, because it was fuggin free! Well, it is free but you gotta own both classic titles. How does this fare? Well...
The gameplay of SS Revolution are like any other Serious Sam game: shoot enemies, get new weapons, shoot more enemies, kill a boss, you get the idea. Sometimes you can get a friend or family member to help out with slaughtering mass hordes of enemies with a minigun. Graphics? Same as the classic games. Old, but impressive for the time....and this time with OpenGL.
As for Revolution itself, the new Steam-based features are pretty cool; with leaderboard support, achievements and Workshop, and more streamlined multiplayer. Of course, seeing how this is a Early Access game, I noticed a rather odd bug where the Workshop items wouldn't load, but it might be because I'm not loading them right or it really is a bug, but eh. <.<
Still, if ya want a dose of nostalgia get this game! I sincerly can't wait for the full release and maybe hear John J.♥♥♥♥♥♥s secksy voice in the new campaign mode, lol.

Fans of Croteam did something great. They combined 2 old games, and added alot of new content to it!
So, what's this?
This is the bundle of the first 2 Serious Sams with more abilities, such as multiplayer coop/pvp, and workshop with maps, weapons and characters!
This game may look old, and it feels old, but its also very fun.
This is something that you should try if you are a Serious Sam fan, or if you simply played the latest next-gen games, and want something different.

SSR is an enhanced re-release of both encounters of Serious Sam 1. This was done for numerous reasons, one of the biggest being how SS1's multiplayer servers were taken down by Gamespy.
SSR features a very large amount of levels, workshop support, 64 bit support and numerous other things. I could go into depth about what made Serious Sam great but fundamentally, you have to play it to see why.
The strengths of Serious Sam could easily be compared to games like Doom or Quake. In that it is the level design and enemy placement that makes it unique and stand out. Every enemy in Serious Sam by themselves are♥♥♥♥♥♥easy to kill. However when the level throws hundreds of them at you, you start noticing just how hard the game is. It is a very rewarding game, and truly one of the best examples of a "classic FPS"
Of course if you don't wanna play alone there's 16 player coop, and deathmatch. With the many varied levels of the first and second encounters, and the hundreds more due to arrive on the workshop. Serious Sam Revolution is one of the best ways to spend 10$ on Steam.
Or you could just buy SS Gold, you get it for free there. Jus' saying...

Smite joined the moba scene and brings its own features like third person camera view. They are themed around gods and do design most of their gods on what they find on them. They have six game modes, each with its own first win of the day bonus. Generally I would mention things similar to League of Legends as I think it is the easiest to explain things in a short matter.
Arena mode is practically like the constant fighting mode where you are in a small map and kind of test all your gods here and try whatever builds. This is pretty much the shortest game mode where lots of team fighting happens. 5 Players on each team.
Joust 3v3 mode has a map design closer to ARAM from League of Legends with two side paths which are kind of like the jungle where the buffs are just sitting there. 3 Players on each team. There is also Joust 1v1 ranked for those who want to duel other players which I think is nice but not perfect.
Conquest mode is the Summoner's Rift of Smite. This is the mode you want to learn really well if you want to be competitive in this game. It has a gold fury(dragon), fire giant(baron), jungle,  an outer and inner turret but no base turret as they are replaced by phoenix that can attack, and the nexus is a titan which fights back. 5 Players on each team.
Assault mode is the random god selection and one lane...just like League of Legends ARAM. Never been fond of this mode personally as sometimes there is just a lot of doing nothing if the team is passive. 5 Players on each team
Siege mode is an unique mode I have not seen from other MOBAs. There is a jungle and two lanes and a bar that summons a super minion called a juggernaut that is able to tank lots of dmg to help push the wave. There is a portal close to spawn that opens when a juggernaut is alive to instantly teleport there. There is a big jungle boss that when defeated will always spawn a juggernaut so you can even have two out at once if planned well. 4 Players on each team.
Lastly there is the Match of the Day(MOTD) mode. This mode changes EVERYDAY. The rules in this mode, map it is played on, and gods playable change daily. If you ever played URF mode in League of Legends, this mode can also have that too. Also to add, sometimes you can have duplicate gods for more fun. This mode does not record any matches in your history and does not earn any points towards your god played. # of players per team vary.
+Third person view more appealing to new players as it feels more immersed into the gameplay
+Lots of different modes that is played all the time unlike dominion/twisted treeline in league thats not played often
+MOTD adds more fun
+Is pretty competitive
+Modes for all sizes of parties
+Events all the time to give out gems (Approximately 2 dollars per 100 gems USD)
+Option to buy all gods for life including all future gods that come out for $20 USD
+Icons/achievements for those who just love competing it
+Gods are awesome(where the bee god come from..?)
+Voice Guidance System(VGS) which are like radio commands for everything(Standard in communication)
-Due to third person view more communication is needed sometimes to make up for the gap of information
-Same frustrations you can get from playing League
-Dodging queue = 30m penality
-Skins are just okayish
-No crossplatform so you can't pwn your console friends
All in all, Smite is definitely a great game and still kind of new to the scene if compared to League of Legends but it is worth trying out if you're into MOBAs.

EDIT: Patch dropped today on 18th of December, 2014, constant framedrops from 91fps (where it was locked before, and stayed at with my 3570k & GTX 760), all the way down to 35fps at times, lag is still as wild as ever. On the brighter side, some of the guns that were super bad are now actually usable and skill based matchmaking, which was hideously broken, was removed.
One step forward, six back. This game is dead to me.
No dedicated servers meaning CONSTANT connection issues, "Skill"-based matchmaking (aka. if you had a KDR above 2 in the previous lobby, you WILL get matched up with prestige master tryhards, even if you just had one single lucky game), an "OK" campaign (boring storyline and characters, but atleast the shooting is fun), Sledgehammer Games is very secretive and silent about this game and upcoming patches.
All this being said, i would love this game to death if they only added dedicated servers and removed the "skill"-based matchmaking. The gunplay is fun, twitchy, fast, as CoD should be, but the added mobility just adds a whole different level of fun to the game. You can actually jump away from gunfire if you are being shot at, which just blew my mind, compaired to old CoD's where the first person who shot won the gunfight 110% of the time.
I'll leave this review with a "Would not Recommend" for now, since there are other FPS games out there that you could be playing instead of this. I will, however, change this review to a positive one if Sledgehammer adds dedicated servers and tweaks the game some more.

Imagine you're walking down a hidden tunnel with some loot at the end, when suddenly you hear something nearby. You look to your left, and see a huge boulder coming towards you! You try to run away, but this is no Indiana Jones movie. Instead, the boulder smashes right into you, and you die a horrible death, because this is Dark Souls.
When fighting tough enemies, you have to get to know their attack pattern. For example, you might think that enemy's third swing of his sword will be easy to dodge, and you rush to attack him from behind, as he swings forward. When you're about to hit him in the back, he whirls around as he swings, as if anticipating your strategy, and kills you... because this is Dark Souls.
Yes, you will die, over and over and over, much like the trailer leads you to believe. But the fun is learning from your mistakes, getting better and better at the game, crushing enemies which you once thought were nearly unbeatable. On top of that, the atmosphere is beatiful and eerie, with hidden lore all over. There's plenty of content, too.
As long as you have the patience to learn from your mistakes, and are willing to die repeatedly, this game is amazing. I can genuinely say it's one of the best I've ever played.

The game for me was an improvement over the first dark souls, but not by a whole lot. The funny part is that the game is too easy (downright a joke in co-op, still easy solo), but people experience different challenges so don't take my word for it.
My only real complaint was what they did to the co-op, mainly towards the timer limit. While happy that you could still summon people in places that had no bosses in, I was quite annoyed when playing with friends and all of a suddon, my buddy disappears when we're charging at enemies. It hasn't ruined it for us and I can understand why they did something like that.
In terms of gameplay, it's pretty similar to the first. I enjoyed some of the weapons that I could play around with along with many other features that make this game less hateful towards people who screwed up their stats. I've only encountered three bosses that were recycled but were given something slightly new so they weren't complete copies, so that's alright in my books.
Other than that, everything that was presented here was better than that of the first dark souls. To the people who complain about the keyboard & mouse control, I was annoyed of it at first, but I figured out solutions and eventually grown to actually like it. I just get annoyed by the still "xbox" functions when trying to perform a task, like scanning through information on the menu. I'm always forced to look at my keybinds or slam every key on the board. A minor issue, but it was expected.
Do I recommend this game? Well the review says yes so I'll say yes. Right now though there isn't much pvping going on (since there's a ton of people. I've only been invaded twice and that was in someone else's world) and the game is too easy. Personally, it wasn't anything special to me so I should've waited for the price to drop, but to anyone who loves the series, give this one a go.
Until then, folks!

text: What's not to like ?
SAM HE IS

Alligator Pit manufactures the original in all new light with dazzling new interface and cleaned up visuals. Serious Sam Classics: Revolution revitalizes the classic games taking on similar ideas as the HD remakes by creating a game with cleaner performance.
Serious Sam: Revolution includes the first and second encounters, which means instead of paying $34.00 for both the First and Second Encounter you can get them both for $9.99 (without being on sale). Although, what you are probably wondering is what else is included in Serious Sam Classics: Reovlution? To name a few better graphical options, steam support, new campaigns, new bosses, improved UI, level editors, and much more.
The First Encounter:
For those who already own the first encounter you should probably skip this. This campaign includes thirteen main story levels and two secret levels. All of the levels take place in Egypt and are about the story of how Serious Sam began his quest to save humanity from Metals domination. The original campaign offers hours of gameplay as the levels are incredibly large and filled with secrets. The levels are composed of fighting mass hordes of enemies, solving puzzles, and completing objectives. During the campaign you will fight three bosses: Highlander Aludran Reptiloid, Lava Golem, and Ugh-Zan III. The brilliant group fights and epic boss fights keep you on your toes constantly engaged in a changing environment.
The Second Encounter:
For those who already own the second encounter you should probably skip this. This campaign includes twelve levels (no secret levels), but it also includes the entire campaign from Serious Sam The First Encounter. The campaign is divided across three kingdoms: Mayans, Persia, and medieval Poland. Similar to the First Encounter the second encounter is incredibly long, the levels are large and filled with secrets. The Second Encounter creates even more puzzles, crazier secrets, and throws more enemies at you than imaginable. Not only will you be engaged in all the mysteries abound, but the campaign also provides four bosses: Kukulkan, The Wing God, Exotech Larva, Mordekai the Summoner, and The Ram-God. The Ram-God is from Legend of the Beast DLC, which I assume is going to be implemented into Serious Sam Classis: Revolution.
Bright Island:
I have no information on this campaign, as it is not available in the early access beta.
Space Crusader (Possible Additional Campaign):
This campaign will include the following levels: Water Planet, Lava Planet, Green Planet, Ice Planet, Tropic Planet, and Rock Planet. Although none of this is mentioned, there are hints that this is being implemented based on the screenshots. The screenshots show that they may finally implement the scrapped levels and weapons from the Original Serious Sam. One of the weapons in the screenshots is the Ghost Buster (it looks like it shoots electricity) which was never implemented in the original campaign. it looks like this weapon is being used on the Rock Planet, which is one of the many various planets that was never included in the Serious Sam Campaign. The original campaign would have been over double the size if they finished developing most of the levels they had planned, but for various reasons they were cut. This makes me hope that this edition is finally fulfilling the original dream for Serious Sam and bringing the campaign in its full glory.
The actual quality of the textures is the same as you would see in the HD remakes, although what Serious Sam Classics: Revolution offers is more than just a HD texture experience. It provides modern day graphical elements including: lens flares, fog, object bending, object translucency, smoother particle animation, haze, high resolution reflections, better portal animations, cleaner lighting, higher shading controls, and more. You can see all of these in action by checking out the Technology Test, which provides you with clean visuals of how these will be seen when implemented into the new campaign.
Finally Serious Sam will have access to the workshop, and proper steam servers. The game is supposed to offer up to 42-player multiplayer and even support split screen. The game will come with a level editor, so if they don’t come out with space crusader or sky city someone will.
Serious Sam Classics Revolution has been out now for almost two-half weeks, since then there has been a bundle of added content to the workshop. These include remodeling of textures, multiplayer maps, and even a custom campaign. SSCR has a lot of to offer, and if the community support continues in this fashion this will be an amazing addition to the series.
At this current point Serious Sam Classic: Revolution is not complete, but lets be honest Croteam and Devlover Digital completed Serious Sam HD in a timely manner; I am sure that you will not be waiting forever, unlike some Early Access Games. This game has a lot of potential with its new graphics engine, level editor, providing the original campaigns, better menu UI, cleaner animations, steam support, and so much more. I would buy this game at full price, but on sale it’s like you are robbing Croteam.
Pros:
+Great new OpenGL shaders and 64-bit support to create a much cleaner and graphic intensive game.
+Steam workshop support
+Steam servers for multiplayer (supports up to 42 players)
+Includes Serious Sam First and Second Encounter
+New Survival Mode
+Already mention of new Bright Island Campaign
+A level editor, so you can go crazy and make your own Serious Adventures
+Loads of enemies and bosses
+Lots of guns to choose from
+Already downloaded my first custom campaign, thanks Workshop support!
Cons:
-Its early access

This game is for you if:

Smite joined the moba scene and brings its own features like third person camera view. They are themed around gods and do design most of their gods on what they find on them. They have six game modes, each with its own first win of the day bonus. Generally I would mention things similar to League of Legends as I think it is the easiest to explain things in a short matter.
Arena mode is practically like the constant fighting mode where you are in a small map and kind of test all your gods here and try whatever builds. This is pretty much the shortest game mode where lots of team fighting happens. 5 Players on each team.
Joust 3v3 mode has a map design closer to ARAM from League of Legends with two side paths which are kind of like the jungle where the buffs are just sitting there. 3 Players on each team. There is also Joust 1v1 ranked for those who want to duel other players which I think is nice but not perfect.
Conquest mode is the Summoner's Rift of Smite. This is the mode you want to learn really well if you want to be competitive in this game. It has a gold fury(dragon), fire giant(baron), jungle,  an outer and inner turret but no base turret as they are replaced by phoenix that can attack, and the nexus is a titan which fights back. 5 Players on each team.
Assault mode is the random god selection and one lane...just like League of Legends ARAM. Never been fond of this mode personally as sometimes there is just a lot of doing nothing if the team is passive. 5 Players on each team
Siege mode is an unique mode I have not seen from other MOBAs. There is a jungle and two lanes and a bar that summons a super minion called a juggernaut that is able to tank lots of dmg to help push the wave. There is a portal close to spawn that opens when a juggernaut is alive to instantly teleport there. There is a big jungle boss that when defeated will always spawn a juggernaut so you can even have two out at once if planned well. 4 Players on each team.
Lastly there is the Match of the Day(MOTD) mode. This mode changes EVERYDAY. The rules in this mode, map it is played on, and gods playable change daily. If you ever played URF mode in League of Legends, this mode can also have that too. Also to add, sometimes you can have duplicate gods for more fun. This mode does not record any matches in your history and does not earn any points towards your god played. # of players per team vary.
+Third person view more appealing to new players as it feels more immersed into the gameplay
+Lots of different modes that is played all the time unlike dominion/twisted treeline in league thats not played often
+MOTD adds more fun
+Is pretty competitive
+Modes for all sizes of parties
+Events all the time to give out gems (Approximately 2 dollars per 100 gems USD)
+Option to buy all gods for life including all future gods that come out for $20 USD
+Icons/achievements for those who just love competing it
+Gods are awesome(where the bee god come from..?)
+Voice Guidance System(VGS) which are like radio commands for everything(Standard in communication)
-Due to third person view more communication is needed sometimes to make up for the gap of information
-Same frustrations you can get from playing League
-Dodging queue = 30m penality
-Skins are just okayish
-No crossplatform so you can't pwn your console friends
All in all, Smite is definitely a great game and still kind of new to the scene if compared to League of Legends but it is worth trying out if you're into MOBAs.

The game offers pretty much all it advertised, something I thought rather rare for a 5 € game.
You're pretty much thrown into the post-apocalyptic world unawares, unequipped, climbing out of your Vault (where have I seen this before?) and completely unprepared for the horrors outside. Thankfully, the game's first tutorial run provides an easy crash course into the game world and mechanics, first strolling you thru combat, party interactions, building bases and trading and so forth.
You'll soon be on your way to building your own post-apo settlement to your own whims, within certain limitations. In addition to your zombie neighbours (colour-coded for your convenience), you'll be setting up diplomatic relations with other settlements in the neighbourhood, with various shantytown or lone survivors out in the boons.
What I did like about the game world was the surprising outcomes and twists in quests- instead of plain boring fetch quests, you can sometimes blunder right into a moral dilemma that needs to be solved on the spot, usually either resulting in placating hostiles, or turning previously friendly forces into hostiles, or score some extra loot or survivors for your settlement.
So, I was somewhat pleasantly surprised when I was tasked with 'wiping out Looters' (the staple of the post-apocalyptic quest world), and instead of brutally gunning everybody down, I was given the choice of sparing a survivor of the group, recruiting them for my cause, instead of persisting in the silly tradition of game foes have of fighting to the death, even against unwinnable odds.
Another time, I was sent to kill looters who stole food from a settlement- only to find out the truth to the matter was not all black and white, as the quest giver had originally let on.
Overall, the game is no State of Decay, Dead State, Rebuild: Gangs of Deadsville or Project Zomboid, but it has it's moments- the combat mechanics tend to be very twitchy, with split seconds to open fire on the Infected, as they barrel down on you from the desert with a hankering for survivor flesh. The infection mechanic is pretty simple- you get bit, you gotta get an antidote. Different strains of the disease have different germination times, with the worse strains taking down the host in minutes, requiring survivors to have the proper antidote at hand, or succumb to the disease themselves. Ammo is usually pretty abundant, and you even score 10.000 pistol rounds in the first hour of the game, so you are unlikely to run out of ammo for the basic shooter during your first days. By day 5, I had enough ammo to spare, equipping most of my resource mules with shotguns, my main character with a automatic rifle and farmers and builders with pistols.
Instead of bottlecaps, food and water, your main currency in the wasteland is gold, which is surprisingly abundant in spite of the whole apocalyptic scenario. I found this somewhat funny that while the game makes it clear that paper money is worthless, the concept that the new economy would be based on a non-essential luxury item is kind of a strange notion. Still, it's no a big deal- you'll end up doing more barter than plain gold trading most of the time, anyway.
So, to summarize:
PROS:
+ Freebuild of your own settlement, within some limitations
+ Additional diplomacy and unexpected realism with some sidequests, moral dilemmas
+ Game's difficult, but does not punish you horribly
+ You can delegate resource fetching, farming, building
+ Survivor AI is not completely helpless if left to their own devices. Pathfinding is decent.
CONS:
- The minimap and survivor topdown view are much too close, even on 1920x1080 resolution, giving the game a 640-x480 look.
- Sometimes survivor messages on the right zoom past at astounding speeds, and you miss whatever tooltip or notice was in question.
- Your survivors are practically blind, barely able to see ten feet in any given direction, so they'll constantly get bushwhacked by super-fast, feral zombies until the route is cleared with buckshot, which brings me to...
- Fast undead. Combat is arcade-y, twitchy, sometimes almost Press 'X' not to die.
- Survivor animations on walk and run are a bit wonky.
- Molotov aiming is a game of chance.
- Some of the music tracks are really tiring. Others, not so bad.
Still, for five bucks, this game is not a bad investment, and probably a good diversion to anyone else who enjoys zombies and town management mixes.

*DISCLAIMER* I am yet to play through Voices from the Sea - Plus, and I will update this review when I have done so. :)
Voices from the Sea is a truly incredible and sweet visual novel.
Voices from the Sea is a short story about a young boy named Cantus. Cantus meets Maris, the blue haired, mysterious girl. Cantus is a moody introvert, he enjoys being alone, and dislikes human interaction. But that all changes when he meets Maris, the cheerful, always happy, and playful girl by the sea.
Cantus regularly visits the beach alone, until he finds Maris, who seems to appear out of nowhere. Maris sparks Cantus' feelings and breaks him out of his emotional shell, his sea shell. :3
This is a quite shorter visual novel than most, but it has an excellent story, and I found it very appealing. The art of the game is truly stunning in comparison to most 'free-to-play' novels, which really makes this game for me. Each piece of the soundtrack is excellent, and they all fit into their corresponding scene. There are only very few characters, which leaves lots of time to connect with each and everyone, may it be; Cantus, Maris or Cantus' Mother.
This story should never be spoilt, as the ending will truly break your heart. I was definitely touched, and just had to play through again. I enjoyed this game very much and appreciated every single bit of it.
I would rate this 10/10, but as of now, there is no sequel, so a 9.5/10 will have to do.
Definitely install this game, as it is truly, life changing.

Fat Chicken is an interesting twist on the strategy genre.  It's made by some industry vets who have worked for Insomniac Games, Red Storm Entertainment, and Westwood Studios.  The creative director was heavily involved in the Command and Conquer series (a personal favorite of mine in the strategy genre) and the experience behind this title shows.  You spend each mission trying to make as much money as possible beefing up farm animals (including poultry as the name suggests) using towers to fatten up, genetically enhance, water, and medicate your animals.  While I have not experienced all of the perks or upgrades yet (I am still in the process of finishing the game) I would like to mention that you are not limited to just a few tower options.  Special skills and tower upgrades are available.  It's got learning curve that makes it easy to get into and a lot of ways to get the most money and meat out of your animals.  This is a definite buy for originality, personality, and just plain fun.

I like this game, alot. It is however far from perfect and yes as others have stated it does have bugs.
Firstly let me say that I am an avid tower defence genre fan, I think its fair to say that over many years I have probably played 75% of all flash tower defence games ever made and about 50% of all retail ones.
Fat chicken has a simple objective, get your livestock from their pens to the processing plant, keep them alive and fatten them up as much as possible without killing them or letting them starve before they reach their impending doom.
Kind of sounds grizzly doesn't it, well you might think from the sounds of it animal rights groups would be all over this game, and they would ... if they had not played it. Unlike most tower defence games this one has a "lite" story that I shall not ruin for you, needless to say that it has a clear moral and ethical tale to tell. Which I might add is done very well and in a light hearted manner, and clearly shows that if you want to get a message across and make people listen then you have to make it fun and entertaining, Fat Chicken manages this on both counts.
The game isn't that long and achievements can all be obtained within 8 hours.
The graphics do the job well
Sounds effects are very good quality.
Music is highly annoying after a short period but can thankfully be turned off.
The bugs :
The most common is that the wave counter and cash $$ indicator stop updating and the only way to force it to update is to press "esc" this causes it to update to what it should be but still does not contine to update to live stats. As a result if this bug happens during a level you will have to press "esc" every so often.
The key cause I have found of causing this bug are the number of active hired hands on screenonce you go beyond around 8-10 it causes this bug to happen, also having more than 9-10 starts to cause slowdown although this is minimal except foe one level, the last level.
*** SPOILER WARNING ***
The Final level of the game is very bugged. Passed wave 5, UFO's and Protestors spawn but do not move or infact do anything, if you have protestors effecting a tower at the point this happens you can not clear the protestor with security, this effectivly locks the tower for the rest of the game. UFO's can still be shot down if within range but they just stop moving and newly spawned ones do nothing and just stil at the worm hole.
The first time I played the last level the camera locked onto the CEO and no matter what I did. I could move the camera but as soon as I let go of the mouse, the camera jumpped right back to centering on the CEO.
Strangly enough these bugs actualy made the final level much easier than I assume it should be, no protestors of UFO's to deal with for more than half the game .... bonus !
The game was easily enjoyable enough for me to spend 12 odd hours writing a guide for this game as well as obtaining all its achievements.

++PROS++
- Feels like a complete game.
- Lots of 80s & 90s references to get yourself giddy with nostalgia.
- Fully destructible terrain (much better than Battlefield).
- Local CO-OP (so many games lack this!)
- Lots of explosions if you love your action games.
- You will gain a sense of patriotism after each level (a.k.a. you will genuinuely feel satisfied for completing each level).
- There's enough variety within each level to keep your interest.
- Plenty of characters to play as (with more on the way).
- The developers are planning more features for the game (continued support basically).
- If you love making maps, there is a level editor.
--CONS--
- This is currently an Alpha build (as I write this review) and some features are currently limited. If you're skeptical, do not buy.
- Like with any Early Access title, there are some bugs (trigger activations on custom maps is one I'm aware of).
- Not all characters are equal, and it will be trial and error when you discover new ones.
- You may become frustrated from dying other simple things (e.g. falling off the first cliff, repeatedly).
- You may become frustrated when your bullets hide any on-coming projectiles from the enemy; thus dying, again.
- The premise of the game is pretty much the same for all levels; jump in and shoot the bad guys. If you're not a huge fan of repeatitive action games, this may not be for you.

Ley Lines is, to be frank, not a good game.
It has some pretty good ideas; the "powers" that you aquire, the creature/character design (even if it's very basic) and the story has promise as well. However, it is let down by poor execution. The mechanics are basic and yet don't feel very good. Especially the jumping lacks the "snappiness" of a more polished platformer, and it can be hard to get a feel for your character's movements. The shooting also lacks that same quality, it feels a bit floaty.
The puzzle design is somewhat poor, mainly because the level design is really lackluster; half the environments feel like they were just "put there" to serve the puzzles, instead of feeling like an actual world. The game gives you a set of different powers, that you activate by walking into different colored fields. This would be a decent idea, except the game is way too short and therefore dumps them all in your lap, which makes the following puzzles too simple and/or annoying to solve.
In many aspects, I feel like this game suffers from a lack of time investment. If the game was longer, all of these concepts that were thrown into the game could've been more fleshed out, more meaningful and more refined. The powers, the puzzles, the creatures, the mechanics... and most of all, the story. The ending to this game is actually very well done, it has a grand scope and it's clear that the developers have a sense of how to make a dramatic scene. But again, since the game is so short, you never have time to be invested in the grand story that they try to present, so in the end, it all falls flat. For this short of a game, you need a small scale story, otherwise it just comes out lackluster.
In summary, this game is half-baked (if even that) and is probably not worth playing. I do see some promise in it though, and I hope that the developers can use that promise to make a more polished game in the future.

I write reviews to all of the games I play. But I WANT to write a review for this one. This game is amazing. Pros-cons are below. I don't want to compare but I can't help myself, this game is what No Man's Sky should have been. It has every aspect that I expected NMS to have. Not neccessarily saying NMS is a bad game, it is fun while it lasts, but that game suffered from false advertising to build up hype and generate sales on release. Moving on before this turns into a NMS review.
Astroneer instead, has several features that I honestly expected from NMS:
+ terrain manipulation: Dig holes in the ground or in walls, inside caves or on mountains. Shape the terrain to your liking. Dig as deep as you want.
+ resource collection on planets: Different resources lie on different planets, you have multiple uses for all of them. Sometimes you need to refine the resource in order to be able to use it. You can get stranded on a planet if you're not prepared for it, simply because the planet lacks said resource.
+ energy: You need energy to do stuff. You run out of energy, or you can work towards not running out of it. There really are multiple ways to get energy; through different devices and resources.
+ building vehicles: Seriously how does a game like NMS lack the ability to build your own space ship? Well, here you can. And you can add all of the resources and extentions you want to add to it, provided you have the neccessary space.
+ base building: How does a game like NMS prevent you from building a base on a planet? Well here you can. You can build on any planet you land. There are currently 6 different building types (which I figure more will come), all with different functionalities, and you need all of them at some point.
+ land vehicles: Build your own customized rover or truck from the vehicle bay. Just like with the spaceship, you can put stuff on your rover or truck that you think is neccessary (like solar panels, storage, habitat, or simply resources to build somewhere else on the same planet).
+ more on energy: All vehicles and buildings run with energy, even your suit/tool
+ research: The only way to upgrade your tech tree and to build better stuff is to do research. You can't build anything aside from the basics unless you research it first. Research "balls" are scattered or hidden around on planets. You find them and bring them back to base to research them and see what it contains.
+ natural hazards: I really believe they add to the game. They prevent it from becoming a boring senseless exploration game. For example, after you set up the basic buildings, you will need more advanced resources, like ores. Well that crap only grows down in the caverns so you need to go down there, but there is hostile plant life in there. Oops, suddenly you need to either steer clear of them and create an alternate route to whatever it is that you are seeking, or destroy them by deforming the terrain under their roots. There are also massive creepy storms. I'll leave that to you to experience, because that was one of the best experiences I have ever come across in a video game.
Now as with every game, this game has negative aspects which all of them are here simply because this game is in extremely early development stage, not because of developmental mistakes or anything.
- Hazards I mentioned above are very limited in number for now, I don't know if I've come across all of them but there are storms, gassy plants, needle plants and passive but giant ground worms. I might have missed one or two maybe. But this is pre alpha and this content is the placeholder that represents dangers of fronteering.
- There are only 6 planets for now to explore (they all have different environments). And you can't leave the system nor are you capable of building a ship that has the required parts for deep space travel. I'm not even sure if galaxial travel will be a thing, but if it was it would be awesome.
- 4 player limitation? (Soon to be removed)
- research is randomized right now, but it's soon to be removed as well. A point based system for research is coming.
- only 2 land vehicles and 2 space vehicles to build.
- hunger and food system is something I am really looking forward to but it's not here yet.
- not much aim unless you are into this kind of thing. Definitely no story or objectives for now. Risk of boredom for the casual player.
- I can't think of anything else for now. These are the biggest cons in my eyes. You may want to check different reviews for the different troubles people experience.
So there are the cons. Well, what do you expect from a "PRE"-alpha game? Fully fleshed out features with a story? No bugs or crashes? That's not how pre alpha games work. If those are what you are looking for, this is not the game for you. Wait for full release. What I can guarantee you (if you are into games with this premise of space exploration, planet colonization, tech tree and resource collection) you will have a lot of fun hours with it.
And what I also can guarantee you is that this, for now, has been one of the most stable early access games that I have ever played. I haven't crashed yet or came across a big bug. On top of that, the game runs butter smooth. Now I had played a previous version at my friend's place, a muuuch earlier version and that version ran bad. Not only I had crashed multiple times but I did come across a lot of bugs. It also ran really slow on a 16gb ram machine. So you can see how far they've come on their initial release, and this is just starting.

This game is basically dark souls with a few things taken and a few things added, so it's still dark souls and thus still good. Now here's what I don't like.
They made it so that the monsters will eventually go away forever if you kill them enough times (which in some cases is a plus). But in trade you can't farm monsters effectively anymore (which is a big minus). They also made it so that you lose max health every time you die and humanity giving items are limited. Now I hope I'm not alone in this, but part of the reason I liked dark souls is because it was hard, but it was also effectively consequence-free when you consider things long-term.
Sure you lost all your souls and humanity when you died but you could always go out and farm them back which gave the game a nice pace. I never felt like I shouldn't go explore there or try jumping off a cliff here, though in hindsight the second was probably pretty dangerous. However in Dark Souls 2 I feel like I'm being restricted. "Better not explore there or jump off a cliff here, I have 24,000 souls and if I die I may lose them forever because I can only grind in a limited capacity".
I do recommend buying this but I recommend making two characters. Your first character should be an all-holds-bared adventurer who jumps off every cliff and explores every crevice ignoring the danger and consequences. When you're done with that go in with your serious combat character once you know what's where. Oh but don't be a swordsman cause one thing they didn't fix from dark souls in this sequel is that dual wielding still sucks.

Although non-graphical peak and the replay value is not high, Fat Chicken is still a very attractive game and a new style of play, worthy of the effort out of an independent development. Fat Chicken is a good choice for entertaining after a period of study and work stress.

Fat Chicken is exactly what I expected going into it: a cutesy, fairly easy TD game with a slightly unique concept. Despite the fact that you're fattening up animals instead of killing them, it plays almost exactly like any other TD game on the market. Here are my main criticisms of this game:
- Really easy and shallow. Most tower placements are no-brainers and the game never puts up much of a fight, even though the final mission initially seems impossible. Getting three stars on every level isn't hard at all.
- Too short. After the main campaign, there aren't any "bonus" levels, or ideally, way harder versions of all the existing levels. When I finished, I wanted more.
- Occasional bugs, such as security guards failing to chase away protestors and a MurderBux counter that stops updating (both of these happened in the final stage by the way.) However, I'm extremely forgiving about this kind of thing and considering the size of the developer and how recently it came to Steam, the level of bugs is actually impressively low.
Despite that, I enjoyed Fat Chicken. I'm a sucker for cutesy stuff like this and the music is actually kinda catchy. I'd recommend this game to casual players specifically, as hardcore players like myself will ironically be hungry for more after completing the campaign.

Reverse tower defense? What? That's exactly it! In Fat Chicken, instead of warding off a throng of enemies, you want to fatten up livestock and welcome them into your slaughterhouse as bloated and fat as possible! The concept may sound disturbing, but it's so silly and exaggerated that you can't help but chuckle. As a matter of fact it was the sheer level of ridiculous that drew me in! The graphics are pleasant and hilarious (gotta say, my first exploding cow absolutely floored me!) There's a wide variety of challenging and different levels, and you can choose your upgrades as you earn enough stars to buy them. I love being able to re-spec my tower upgrades depending on the level. I love that the 3-star challenge changes from level to level, adding a challenging element and making you think! I've gotten hours and hours of fun out of this game! Good work guys!

An awesome reverse tower defense game!  I am thouroughly impressed with the mechanics and the atmosphere the game provides for the player.  Sure, the subject matter would probably have PETA breathing down their necks (or an equivilent like the protesters in the game) but for me this game was wonderful entertainment!  Just the right amount of challenge to really get my brain going.

Tower defense is as tower defense does. A cute appearance masks the dark undertones that replaces weapons with stations to force feed livestock. There's a social commentary  buried that toys with lives in a cold, capitalist world. Still, challenges of puzzling buildings on an assembly line stay mostly the same, which drops the freshness of this product considerably.

We were pleasantly surprised at how much fun AND challenging Fat Chicken actually is. The developers did a great job allowing the player to select from multiple Powers and Upgrades. Of course, you’ve got to earn your way in order to afford them and that might be a fun challenge as well. The game gets you thinking strategically as far as where to place your towers and human helpers as well as how much to feed or not to feed, use growth hormones, or not – you basically have to learn your way around the game in order to make sure that your livestock does not perish before they hit the factory.  We found ourselves playing each level several times in order to gain all three stars and even on Easy level setting, it was not that easy. You also get a cast of Heroes to select, each one costing a bit of change, but once you earn them – your life might get a little bit easier. In addition, the tutorial/hint snippets are highly useful so make sure to pay attention. Expect to spend extra time going through all of the stages, but be forewarned – the game is highly addictive! Reactions to this title remind me of the Batman Arkham Knight release, although not as hefty. Both are excellent games who had a hickup start.
Sadly, most of the negative reviews don't even list the hardware used.
As with Arkham City I'm lucky this time. I'm running the game on 1920x1080, high settings but for textures (very high) and shadows (medium), HBAO+ on, 1xFXAA.
The game runs fine enough (40-60fps) although not exactly smooth (as Doom), no crashes, no serious frame drops so far.
That much about the performance. About the game itself: I love it. It has the same great, at times uncanny, steampunk atmosphere as Part 1. The wider and much more vertical maps make the world more believable, this city feels like one. If you are a sucker for the story as I am: there's a ton of lore items in form of books, letters and audio logs. The new skills allow some very creative mayhem, especially Emily's skills offer some nasty combos. The freedom of how you approach the game ranging from low chaos ghost (never heard, never seen, no kills) to high chaos lunatic (violent killing spree) make replays interesting enough.
Presentation in both sound (orginal Thief/Garrett-voice Stephen Russell for Corvo!) & graphics are excellent. The style may not be to everybody's taste but at no point I'd say it looks outdated. If you feel insecure about buying it after all the negative reviews, wait for update.
The game itself I can recommend, it's one of the best titles this year.

Borderlands... though I sadly never played the first part (I know I probably should do that in time), I got a full taste of the sequel.
The Story:
You are playing one of four Vault Hunters (with DLC six), which were originally hired by Handsome Jack to find the Vault, but the realized too late that it was a trap set up by him. You barely survive his attack and wake up to your soon-to-be "best friend", Clap-trap. He shows you the way to Sanctuary, a City full of revolutionaries that oppose Handsome Jacks ways. And with the help of the old and new characters, you start that revolution.
The Gameplay:
As I said, you play as one of six Vault Heroes, who are:
- Axton, who is basically a Soldier with the ability to build turrets and other useful abilities
- Zer0, a "Cyborg Ninja", who has his specifications in Sniping and Close Combat, and stealth abilites
- Maya, who is one of the rare Sirens, with their possibilities such as warping, vacuum-kind-of attacks, and team
supporting abilites
- Salvador, a dwarf with anger problems, who´s main active ability is to wield two guns at once
- Gaige, one of the DLC characters. She has a self-built Robot in her arsenal that can help her in many ways
- Krieg, one of the DLC characters. He is basically a bandit and has his main focus on explosives.
As already said, every character has his own 3 skill trees, which allow you to get a destructive combination. Apart from that this game is pretty RPG like, with a limited option to customize your character, finding weapons, mods, grenades and such. You do side quests to level up and get stronger for the main quests. What I loved about this game are the different damage types for various foes and vise-versa.
And even after you complete the story, there are still DLCs to do and, after you did that, various new game plus modes that let your character level up even more, which gives this game a good replayability.
My opinion:
As I said, I really enjoyed this game story wise and gameplay wise. It´s both humourus and serious. I played it in coop which was even more fun.  All in all I really recommend it, even if you haven´t really played the first part.

Firstly I did recieve this game as a gift from a friend of mine. Take that as you will. If you don't wish to read the whole thing here is the short version. Like exploring? Mining? Minor Crafting? Well buy it. Personally I recommend it if you like those 3 things especially if it involves space exploration.
In the games current state I would say ask yourself if it's worth it. As you can see the game is in it's Pre-Alpha stage meaning bugs here and there and lack of content. I also recommend if you do get it to have some friends to play it with, cause while playing it alone can be a relaxing experience, playing it with friends is one of the better experiences I have had with it. While lately the new content in updates has been minor if any at all, but as someone who went through a year of game design and programming it is not an easy task to make a game. The work the team is getting done is making the game a more enjoyable experience. My cousin and I got this game a few months ago deciding it would be worth supporting (We are both huge fans of space exploration) so when we got it we instantly fell in love with the art style. The songs that play are quite enjoyable as well and really add the the immersion of the game. Now to wrap up my rambling here are some features currently present in the game
Features:
-Exploration
-Crafting(Simple crafting but still)
-Mining
-Online Co-op(Up to 3 other people)
-Terrain adjustment(can also be included with mining)
Now while that may seem like a list of things you would do in Minecraft this game I feel provides a more relaxed atmospheric experience, also a major component of my enjoyment came from the ability to explore different planets.
So again it is all on you, do you want to support a Pre-Alpha space exploration game, If yes buy it, if no don't, if you still aren't sure watch the videos or look up some online. Get an idea of what goes on in the game before making the decision to support it and again it is much more enjoyable with friends.

This game is honestly very good.  You're easily getting a game worth more than the $5 you're paying for it.
What I like about this game is being able to individually control all of your people, giving them jobs, equipping them, etc..  Your man power actually matters in this game instead of them feeling like dead weight like they did in State of Decay.  In SoD you pretty much had to do everything yourself as the player.  In this game, you actually have to delegate orders to ALL of your community members unless you want to run back and forth hauling boards and chicken wire a few at a time.  Your community actually feels like, a, well, community.  It's not unlike in SoD where you radio in for someone to come grab stuff while being arbitrarily limited by the game.  It's the same principle, but a very different execution.  Whereas SoD focuses more on exploration and beating up zombies, Survivalist focuses more on the town building.
You get this game for the awesome town and community building aspect.  If you want to run around slaughtering zombies, there are better alternatives, like State of Decay, because that is not the object of this game.

I Have spent a few good hours on this game and felt it worthy of writing a rewiew. I have enjoyed this title so far, Even thought I feel like the controls are made for a controller more than a keyboard every thing is still responds smoothly. There are a lot of interactions with NPC in this game, some of the dialog is very funny, and what you choose to say can affect the story. I have found this game to be one of those that you better save often or youll find yourself loosing a few hours of game play because you saved three hours before you got infected, or injured. I like the NPC team control in this game. You must keep track of your survivors health and sleep statistics, or at least make sure they have food and water available to eat and drink themselves. You can send survivors in different directions and on different quest at the same time. There is a system that allows you to give orders and the survivors will use their own AI to complete the task given. So far I have one fetching water, one fetching wood, and the other is completeing the story quest. Ammo is sometimes hard to come by in this game and youll need a lot of it to level your firearm skills. Dont allow the infected to bite you as the antigen is hard to come by and is very expensive. I think this game has a neat User Interface it is simple I really enjoy the action camera view in the UI. So far what ive explored of the map is pretty fun, not knowing whats ahead always makes things tense however I feel that the survivors would be able to see a bit further than they are able to in the game, but then they wouldn't have so many suprise infected moments.

Once upon a time, long before Nintendo and Sony, when the "PC Master race" was still in it's larval stage, there was The Bard's Tale. There were no 3D graphics cards, or surround sound features. There was just a glorified text adventure with a few pixels of color to give you an idea where you were, what you were doing, and what that giant robotic scorpion that just destroyed your entire group 'sort of' looked like.
Computer games were more tabletop than arcade - the best parts of them took place entirely in your own imagination. When Wasteland appeared, it was from another world. No wizards and swords and dragons. There were guns, goth chicks who spit on the ground, and horribly demented bad guys named after Donald Duck's nephews. The game only gave you 10 words to describe each and every one of them, but in the world of the imagination, they were tough, gritty, and completely bad♥♥♥♥♥
Technology and the capacity of the human mind to always make things better than they once were has left this classic behind - to the degree that it is now sustained purely by nostalgia than actual contribution. To speak of Wasteland to today's League of Legend's addicts is to listen to the haunting tails of the first appearance of the motorcar, whose alarmly breakneck speed of 10 MPH was fueled by the doomed souls of hell hosted sinners.
So I do recommend this game - but only if you approach it as an automated, self-mastered table top RPG. You will be given brief snippets of data, and your imagination will be expected to fill in the gaps. Essentially, this game is only as amazing as you are willing to make it.

TL;DR
If you've played DS1, this one is a little more refined in gameplay, but suffers a weaker story and atmosphere. It's still completely worth owning and replaying for days on end.
Full Review:
So what is it like compared to DS1? Well DS2 expanded on the gameplay a lot more. There's more stats, more spells, more fluid combat. The challenge is still there. In many ways it is much harder than DS1, especially in the DLC content (which is worth getting BTW, not your typical money grab grool they serve up in other games).
The story is a tad bit weaker, but still interesting.  Basically you end up at Drangleic trying to figure out what happened to the kingdom and its ruler.  There was clearly a war of somekind, and the Curse of The Undead plays its part as well.
The setting for DS2 isn't as strong either. That uneasy feeling of dread you felt in DS1 isnt in this game.
The gameplay is the games strongest feature.  The dungeons to explore, the loot to find, the way you can mold your character. This doesn't differ from DS1 that much, its just greatly expanded on.
The covenants are much weaker this time around however. The rewards for joining/working in a covenants are very underwhelming compared to the work you have to put in. And they don't continually reward you, like you felt in DS1. This causes you to jump from covenant to covenant as you collect what you need.  Or eventually settle on a team to play in for PVP, basically.
The design is still amazing. Poison filled dungeons, volcanic castles, sunken dragon temples...Everything is on an epic scale.  And if you can see a landmark in the distance of the map, chances are you will go there.  The game is beautiful, and the designers give you the chance to explore it.
Messed up something on your first play through? No worries... New Game+ has you covered.  Any sidequests you missed can be done, even more content unlocks each time you play through the game. But at the same time, you're not going to miss anything big if you just want to play a character once.
There is a lot of freedom here, there's a lot of great gameplay.  While its not on par with DS1, the story and lore is still amazing.
Is the game hard?  Well duh.  If you havent played DS1 and you come straight into this, you're gonna be hating life.  There are battles where you go "this is impossible, and stupid." But if you work on it, and get through the game its extremely rewarding.
If you like dark fantasy, dragons, undead, and looting massive dungeons then you need the Dark Souls games in your library.  Dark Souls is a real game, in a crowd of poser bro shooters, and cash cow RPG's.  This is a real game, and it will put you to a real test, and give you a real reward - if you earn it.

It's very good, but not an improvement in every way over the original.
It's still a game about patience, exploration,  and murdering a bunch of stuff.  There's souls to collect, equipment to improve, and blood stains of fallen players everywhere. If you liked the first one, you'll almost certainly like this one.  If the idea of a challenging-but-fair game that isn't a hand-holding power fantasy appeals, you might like this. That said, allow me to blab a little bit about the changes I didn't like.
The biggest step backwards is the level design.  In Dark Souls 1, all the areas were connected and interwoven in interesting ways.  If you saw a bridge early in the game, you would probably get there later.  Dark Souls 2 doesn't do this very much.  The areas feel disconnected, and that makes it feel lazy.  It's like Demon Souls (or Super Mario!), where you've got the separate worlds that are all cool on their own but there's no real connection between them.   Dark Souls 1 made me expect more.
The other step backwards is the story.  I don't think I like it as much as the first one.  It starts off on a bad foot, with two cut scenes and entirely too much dialog and exposition.  My guess is they wanted to be absolutely certain that every new player really got it that their character was undead, and cursed, and undead, and also undead.  Maybe players in the previous game didn't listen to Oscar and got confused? No one's fault but their own, but I guess they wanted to cater to that crowd. But even after that, there are more NPCs and they tend to talk more. They also don't seem to have their own agendas in the same way the ones in Dark Souls 1 did.  Maybe that's fine, but it made it feel more like a traditional RPG where vendors sit around and wait for you to need them.
The bosses also aren't quite as memorable.  In the first one, the big four bosses you were told about in the intro cut scene.  There was a nice build up when you had a showdown with the badass from the opening cut scene. Not so much here.
But that negativity aside, it's still pretty solid.  You still get killed if you're sloppy or careless.  There are traps that will ruin your day if you're not paying attention.  If you like a challenging and rewarding game, it's worth playing.

Amazingly cute and well designed tower defense style game where you are trying to pump up the incoming creatures on the map rather then trying to destroy them.  The reason you ask?  Quite simple... The incoming creatures are farm animals like chickens, cattle, and pigs being processed for human consumption!  Since you get paid by the pound, the fatter these animals are before going into the packing facility, the more money you make!  Don't let them die of hunger, thirst, or alien invasion before they are packaged up and you are rewarded for their weight!
Use the money earned to buy more hormone injection guns, more corn-firing food guns, and antibiotic guns as well as upgrading them all!  Also money earned helps you buy power ups, farm hands, and upgrades.
It's a comical, very cute and amazingly challenging tower defense style game that pokes fun at the sad state that is our current food industry.  It's all about the money in this game, and the animal caring folk need not apply here!
I'd give it an 8/10 for both challenge, originality, and sheer number of options and features... and this game could easily get even better as the game evolves through it's early access process!

I had heard a lot about what a let down this game was and I wasn't going to get it, but I'm actually pretty glad that I did! Don't get me wrong, the performance is definitely not optimized, but it's far from game breaking. There are two things you can do to fix performance issues:
1. It's very important that, until they patch it, you set your advanced video settings to custom and completely disable Anti-Aliasing. Doing this more than doubled my frame rates. I play with everything else on Ultra, besides Viewing Distance which is set on High.
2. Download (for free) "Process Lasso." A part of the problem people are experiencing is due to the game being given low priority in task manager. Process Lasso is a real time optimization utility. You will want to set Dishonored 2 to high priorirty.
I have come across some inconsequential moments where the frame rates have dropped as low as the 30, but this has only happened three times so far and never in the places that matter. The frame rate drops I've experienced have all been outside of combat, not in big areas, but rather in small spaces or indoors where my character is often alone. They also don't last long. Split seconds.
Other than those few hiccups, I've been able to maintain steady 60fps at 1080p HD (on Ultra and I don't even have top of the line hardware). The gameplay itself is great and the combat mechanics, as always, are some of the best. I like the addition of a new character and actually really enjoy her move set.

Wasteland is a product of its own time - low-res graphics, clumsy user interface, and a habit of not exactly telling you how to accomplish things like, say, giving the Visa card to Head Crusher (the game wants you to use one member of your party and put the Visa card on the seat you were previously sitting in opposite of Head Crusher, rather than, say, walking up to him and giving it to him directly).
This was fine back in the day. This is because that game was released in the era of computing known as The Bad Old Days, where you had to manually configure your PCI/ISA cards to avoid IRQ conflicts, where you had to make DOS Bootdisks to free up enough memory just to get the damn video game running, where you could write a little graphical menu in DOS where you could park the heads of your incredibly expensive 10 MB hard drive. You know, just in case the FBI comes around to ask you why you've been pirating so much goddamn software to the rest of your Warez buddies on the BBS networks. Computer users had to put up with a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥just to get games like Wasteland running, and so games like these were walks in the park compared to knowing the exact DOS commands to Telnet into the Matrix or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t like that.
This version of the game runs entirely in a custom emulation environment. It includes a custom soundtrack written by a fan which is pretty cool. The game also allows you to read the paragraphs inside the game (complete with voice overs) when it asks you to read paragraph 38 or another random arbitrary number. The storytelling is pretty good. Other than that, it's pretty much just like the old PC version, which is as accessible to new players as noise music is to regular people. It will definitely make the old, bearded crowd sigh and reminisce about The Bad Old Days.
I recommend you give this about five hours, read a summary and the paragraph book, and then wait for Wasteland 2 to finish up.

I was very surprised by this game. Survivalist is a top down post-apocalyptic RPG similar to State of Decay and Dead State. Set one year into the zombie apocalypse you start off as a wealthy business man with heaps of worthless money who has been living alone in a bunker for a whole year hoping to wait out the apocalypse, but then your bunker supplies unexpectedly ran out. Left with no choice but to venture outside you will encounter other survivors, zombies, looters and so your adventure begins in this zombified desert wasteland.
The game is not perfect but it is still very fun to play. The graphics are pretty dated; they look like The Sims 2 from 2004 level of graphics but with better shadow effects. But this is probably due to the game be ported over from old Xbox 360 hardware, which also limits the frame rate to about 30 so that may turn some people off. Also the aiming is off as you cannot pull off any headshots against your enemies which makes gun combat pretty annoying in early game where your character's firearms skills are low and can lead to some pretty cheap deaths with your characters. Also ammo and supplies are plentiful in this game which can take away some of the hardcore survival aspects of this game.
But the positives out-way the negatives, gameplay is still fun and there is a lot to see and do, there is a good package here for just $5. If you enjoy zombie games like State of Decay which is also similar, then you will have no serious problems with this game.
Survivalist has my seal of approval.

This first-person shooter is packed with action from beggining to end, you get to hail and kill in a wide variety of places and try all kinds of vehicles: boats, motorcycles, cars, planes, armored super suits, you name it.
The EXO's functions are healthily varied: insta-health, magnetic gloves, riot shield, boost jump, drone commanding, invisibility, etc. There's also a perk system and you get to use a different set of EXO skills in every mission; the tactical grenades are varied as well: threat to detect enemies, flash to temporarily blind them and EMPs to screw with electronic-dependent enemies (ASTs, drones). Everything is pretty varied but the weapons, which variety is pretty average; laser (which can only be used like two times in the game), SMG, AR, RPG, pistol, sniper, grenade thrower and that's about it... not many variations or surprises when it comes to this, everything feels pretty standard.
Gunplay is delicious but fairly unrealistic (as usual with CoD games, like some people say), iron sights feel like a requirement because your accuracy will go to hell if you don't use them. There's basically no way to miss your target if you're using iron sights.
There isn't a boss in the entire game (closest thing to it is an AST, which is pretty easy to kill once you find the way) and the story is pretty straight-forward, no optional objectives or side missions. After you finish the campaign, you can replay any level to hunt achievements/collect intel.
Graphics are stunning in this game. Excellent DOF, textures, physics and luminosity; facial animations are top-notch and cutscenes are so well done that they can look like real-life scenes from a proper distance.
Soundtrack is meh, it fulfills its purpose. Unobtrusive and average.
This game is partially lefty friendly.
Let's be honest, this could've been "yet another Call of Duty game" if it wasn't for three things: token female character, boost jumps and good graphics. Still, a pretty solid game with good mechanics and high replayability potential.
Cutscenes are unskippable.
Singleplayer: 8/10 action-packed and fun from beggining to end

+ The gameplay is loads of fun and deeper than I ever would have thought. In a basic sense you are a Slime rancher who goes out and catches a variety of slimes. You then feed them fruits, vegetables, or meat (chicken) which makes the slime create "Plorts" which you can sell and use that currency to build up your farm.
+ I found this game to be very charming and surprisingly relaxing. It is very casual, so you don't have to worry too much about getting killed, and even if something does goes wrong you can easily rebuild in a short amount of time.
+ Visually the game is super cute with adorable slimes with faces, and a very pleasing art style that is colorful and just a joy to explore.
+ "Plorts' are gems that every slime creates. If you feed a slime a plort from a different type of slime it turns into a brand new cross-breed slime. It is so much fun to experiment with different slimes and can be very rewarding too!
+ There is a large variety of things you can purchase at the shops. Upgrades for your character, upgrades for your pens, new pens, farming fields for food, and you can even purchase the ability to unlock brand new areas to explore.
+ The game kinda just throws you in, and allow you to learn and play at your own pace. Normally this would be a downside from my perspective, but Slime Rancher is incredibly intuitive and very easy to learn. You sorta just learn as you go without needing any help or tutorials.
+ Nice relaxing soundtrack

If you haven't bought this game already, you should definitely buy it now. AND if you have the so-called "Destiny" I recommend abandoning it and getting yourself Borderlands 2.
Borderlands 2 is a huge world where you get to explore terrain, kill ♥♥♥♥, and get loot. Never has doing this same thing over and over again been so fun in any other game where you grind as well, since getting legendary items feels pretty satisfying (as well as the occasional pearlescent from the second Ultimate Vault Hunter Upgrade pack, despite half of them being garbage-tier).
Aside from the grinding, the story Borderlands 2 presents is damn good. BL2 has that type of dialogue that you can pop a couple of drinks to and laugh at with your friends, kind of like watching TV. It also presents one of the most (in my opinion) funniest and arguably best antagonist of any video game, Handsome Jack. Unlike most villains who encounter you from time to time without making communication with you between those times, Jack will constantly taunt you, which makes this kind of villain the one that actually pisses you off (in a good way).
The roster includes 6 characters, each of which are all fun to play, and 2 of which are DLC (which are worth buying). Play as Maya the Siren, and you get to lock your enemies in place, and better yet, manipulate them to fight for you. With Axton the Commando, you get yourself a rocket and bullet shooting turret that you could hide under to give you protection whilst fighting alongside it, fighting defensively in one position. With Salvador, the Spanish man that likes to shoot things, you can gunzerk and dual wield any kind of weapon, whether it be a pistol and a shotgun or two rocket launchers (as well as gain alot of your health back and increase your gunzerking with each kill you get, which is the Yipee Ki Yay skill). Play as Zer0, and you have two choices. You can invest in his "Bloodshed" skill tree and melee your enemies to oblivion with your katana, or the "Sniping" tree, which allows you to (probably) one-shot powerful bosses in the game, so long as aiming is your thing. Otherwise Salvador should be better suited.
Play as Gaige the Mechromancer, and get yourself your own mech which you can fight alongside with, as well as have ♥♥♥♥ty Star Wars Stormtrooper aim whilst drastically increasing your damage with the "Anarchy" skill. And lastly, with Krieg the Psycho, you can RELEASE THE BEAST AND GAIN YOURSELF A NEW HUGE HAND AND BUZZAXE AND TURN THE ENEMIES THAT SURROUND YOU INTO NIPPLE SALAD AND THROW BOOM ROCKS WITH THE "LIGHT THE FUSE" THINGY WHILE YOUR IN FIGHT FOR YOUR LIFE AND HAVE SO MUCH JOLLY GOOD TIMES.
11/10, this game is one of moist ones out there, definitely recommend it.

Where do I begin with this game? I first played it on console for roughtly 3000 hours, and then got it on PC when I started PC gaming. Yeah Yeah, I know this is an old game, but personally I think it is still super playable and fun. It is like a fine wine, and has gotten better with age.
As for story, you have your bad guy, wants to take over the world and what not. So it is like every other game right? Wrong. Handsome Jack is by far one of the best villians I have ever seen. He is extremely believable, likeable, and has a very strong charismatic vibe to him. Seriously if you don't like him there is something wrong. I will try to avoid spoilers as much as possible with this. As for the characters you see several old faces if you had the pleasure of playing the first installement of the series. Sadly though you only get to visit 1 location from the old one and that is a very limited sized area. I would have loved to see the old places like the Dahl Headlands and the Rust Commons with the updated graphics and gameplay from this one.
Gameplay is basically like most other FPS games, Firstperson so you cant see your character without mods. It is also an RPG with several different ways you can build your characters and set your skill points, which can change your melee or change up how your special ability works.
Your characters are Axton the commando, Zero the Assassin, Maya the siren, Salvador the gunzerker, Gaige the mechromancer, and Kreig the psycho.
Axton throws out a sentry turret.
Zero goes invisible and can deal out 1 stupidly powerful attack.
Maya locks 1 enemy out of the fight for a short time.
Savador pulls out a second weapon and lays waste to the enemies.
Gaige Summons her trusty rusty deathtrap.
and Kreig goes into a blood thirsty rampage.
OK so I want to make it clear that Gaige and Kreig are DLC characters so you have to pay for them.
The DLC maps are tons of fun and by far my favorite is The Assault on Dragon's Keep.

Well... Wasteland 1. For a game that came out in 1988, this sure has some things going for it. For one, it's the godfather of the Fallout games... but don't let that fool you. First of all, this came out 9 years before Fallout 1, and it shows. Graphics quality is low, of course, and combat is the type of turn based Pokemon had in the first generation, but instead of showing you and your enemy, it just shows a profile of what you enemy supposedly looks like, just to show you something other than text. Second of all, the differences in Fallout and Wasteland are very obvious, story-wise. I'm not going to go into details here, but the apocalypse in Wasteland happened in the late 90's. The 1990's that is. So yeah, that's just some perspective.
Overall... most parts of this game have not aged... well. They haven't aged badly, per se, but they have aged. Graphics quality is low, as you should expect from a game in the late 80's. The combat is, as I said above... iffy. The story, however, is great. The writing is also great. But then, comedy and satire always age relatively well.
For me, having not played this when I was younger like most people who will buy this game (people born in the 80's, or earlier I mean), and only having messed around with it in DOSbox (not a very... shall we say, fun situation), I think it's done well enough over the years for me to say that this is still a good game. The addition of the paragraphs and voice over also make this game so much easier to experience than in DOSbox, seeing how most people don't actually have copies of the original Paragraph booklet anymore.
But yeah. I'm going to say this game is still fun, almost 30 years later, and reccomend it to everyone who wants a taste of what Fallout was before it was Fallout and/or want to experience an old game with some new updates.
