So here I am - heading back home on a bus from school, early 1989. The only real thing on my mind? Firing up the Commodore 64 and rejoining the bunch of Desert Rangers that have just escaped from their first encounter with the Scorpitron. Clips of various calibres were burnt through, LAW rockets fired, two mortally injured - but the team survived. Just.
How had this game got to captivate me so much? To this day, Wasteland ranks as my No.1 game of all time. Not a maybe, not a floating possibility amongst five other great games - but the clear front runner and sole contender. One that I doubt will ever be usurped in the immediate and all-consuming effect that wandering into the radioactive barrens of the American mid-West had on me.
Wasteland is a top-down RPG that follows the 'good guys' of Desert Rangers - attempting to put right the wrongs and work out what strange events are happening in post-nuclear desert around Las Vegas. Fully customisable characters are still fun today, but in late 1988, this was unheard of. Brawlers, pistoleros, ranged specialists to hi-tech geeks were all here - including murderous cyborgs, dodgy gamblers, bar owners and lethal, radioactive vermin. Wasteland introduced the options of restraint, or over-kill - depending on your mood and temperament. Do you carefully take a single shot at your target? Or burst fire of a trio of bullets? Or to hell with accuracy and lead count and simply rip through a magazine? Your ammo, your choice.
A newcomer to Wasteland in 2014 will be woefully unimpressed. What's all the fuss about? It looks archaic has virtually no sound and the main storyline can be completed in a very short time span. But a quarter of a century ago, this game shattered the adventure genre apart and set a whole new level of benchmark. The highly influenced offspring of the Fallout games show plenty of direct lineage back to the original game. But none enthrall in quite the same way that Wasteland did.
Even Steam refers to Wasteland 1 as 'The Original Classic'. For those lucky enough to have been around on its first release - that phrase sums it up perfectly.

This game is a fantastic game. It is technically better than the first game in so many ways.
The combat is fluid and chaotic, the enemies pose a real threat. Every enemy from the first hollow to the bosses can legitimately end you, and will. The atmosphere is dark and despair inducing.
Beautiful environments encase well built levels, and most areas have a charm to them. However, this is also where this game falls a little short. In Dark Souls, the game world felt organic and alive. The areas interconnected in a way that made you feel like it was a cool discovery when you opened a shortcut elevator or back door. Ben "Yahtzee" Croshaw stated what I feel best: "... it looks like they designed the environment first and figured out how you get around in it second." The second game lacks that as much, a lot of the level design FEELS like level design, rather than a castle or a cavern. In Dark souls the world felt more alive with NPCs that moved and breathed and had stories of their own. In this game you get a definite hub area with your own menagerie of collected characters. And once they're in Majula, they NEVER leave.
The game is fantastic. It is a great play and is incredible fun. It is better than its predecessor in many ways, However world design and enemy creativity aren't it. I would recommend this game to anyone who isn't afraid of overcoming a challenge.

It's fun jumping from above and catching enemies by surprise, and playing fast paced cat and mouse dog fights with other players as you hop around from story to story within buildings and structures.
I will recommend this game with the caveat that you will have to deal with technical frustrations. They are barely tolerable. If not for the fresh exoskeleton gameplay I would most definitely not recommend this game. But I support the new gameplay direction for COD and I hope it is here to stay because I am most definitely bored of ground bound COD shooters. At the very least I need vehicle gameplay to keep me interested such as in Battlefield 4. I'll never again be able to play a shooter where you can't leave the ground after playing this one. Sad to see that you can't currently purchase any of the older Fallout games, I decided to give this little gem a try. I've wondered about older, more text-based games and the aforementioned Fallout series grasped my attention and pulled it towards the post-apocalyptic RPG.
Wasteland, like many PC games in the 1980's, seems to warrant more of an adventure through text and its complicated gameplay, rather than its graphics. The game's graphics give you a basic idea of your bearings, but that's about it. Your crew of, at the beginning, four is identified by a single nonmoving sprite, the world moves in semi-real time--where every time you make a move an NPC or a group of them on your screen move as well. The gameplay has many tabletop elements, and uses complicated stat systems for its battles. This can be somewhat frustrating, especially when your teammates come under constant attack and you can't land a single hit. I also feel less in control, as the combat system works by having you select your attacks, then watching it occur next to a portrait of the general enemy type.
The story, though? It's interesting. To make up for the lack of graphics, Interplay managed to put acute detail into the wording of descriptions. Fall into a creek in a small town? It'll describe how you did and how you became embarrassed as kids nearby started laughing at you. Run into the wall of a building? The game will give you a full description of the building and the wall type.
I feel the modernization of the game was welcome. Sure the graphics look a little plastic and odd, but they do the job overall.  I haven't gotten very far, but the outdoor desert theme provides an unsettling ambience for your rangers exploring a desolate wasteland.
On the surface, it's the slight revamping of a complicated, PC RPG which, without a manual, will leave you in a darkness you can never escape. But once you get into it, and begin to understand the wastes and its story, you might be hooked. That is, if you're an intent reader. So, if you're curious about games like Fallout, take a look at this, afterall, FO is Wasteland's spiritual successor.

You can open closed door with the lockpicking ability, or you use the climb skill, or force it open with a crowbar or blow it up with a rocket launcher.
Your group starts with four people and can be extended to seven members by recruiting certain civilians and creatures. And you should do it as fast as possible, because this game has a high and sometimes unforgiving difficulty level.
Most people will be discouraged by the outdated graphics and initially rough gameplay. But if you are willing to give this game a chance, you will experience a classic role-playing game with all its charms and challenges.

Shoot bandits with over-the-top guns, collect loot, and improve character skills while on an incredibly fun quest to find a legendary alien vault.
In Borderlands 2, you will shoot and loot your way across the planet with the help of the cast from the first Borderlands.  Opposing you are hordes of bandits and corporate soldiers.  While most adventure games try to ignore that the protagonist is a homicidal kleptomaniac, Borderlands 2 recognizes and plays off its moral ambiguity.  As in the first Borderlands, the game primarily consists of shooting enemies and hoping they drop good equipment, while building XP to level up your character skills.  Though the game is perfectly playable alone, cooperative play is encouraged by the game design, allowing friends to drop in and out of each other's games at will and without interruption.  The main content of the game took me about thirty hours to get through.  My first playthrough, including downloadable content, took about a hundred hours.
+ same basic gameplay as the first Borderlands, but much more polished story and presentation
+ random loot
+ humor
+ 96.5% more wubwub
+ a good antagonist
+ skill points, interesting skill trees
+ ability to redistribute skill points (encourages experimentation because you're never stuck with a decision)
+ in addition to character-specific skill points, all of your characters share their proficiency points (improved reload speed, greater weapon damage, etc), so playing as any character improves all your characters
+ convenient cooperative play
+ penalty for dying is very low, and the only way to manually save is to leave the game (and the save system saves character state, not world state), encouraging you to just go in with guns blazing
- the downside of the system only saving character state is that if you leave the game during a mission, you will have to start it again from the beginning
- common-grade loot becomes worthless once past the initial stages of the game
- game begins to lose its balance at very high levels
- rare for vending machines to sell anything useful, so mostly just used them to sell old loot

This is my actual play time on this game:  2713h 44m  according to Smite Guru as of this writing.  I think really long reviews are a pain so I'll get right down to it.  This game is a MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) only in 3rd person.  This game is like a mix between your favorite MMORPG and your favorite PVP game.  Most games end on average of about 30 minutes depending on game type, so you never have to devote a nights' worth of time to get anything done either.  I'll list just a few of the Pros and Cons of Smite:
Pros:
- Third Person Perspective
- Incredibly Balanced (69 Gods as of this writing)
- Game is easy to play, but very difficult to master, yet super addictive
- Completely free, you just pay to look cool, or if you want to unlock Gods faster. ($30 for ALL Gods and every God to ever come out, not a bad deal)
- Most abilities are skill based, not locked on
- Devs are very responsive with the community via Reddit, Twitch, forums, etc...
Cons:
- Game can get frustrating at times, sometimes you cant buy a win
- Community can be a bit harsh to new players and seasoned players alike, but hey.. everyone has rough games
- Matchmaking is the biggest problem, especially in ranked games
- Steep learning curve, but if you can get over that, then you're greatly rewarded
- Very few people have the patience to teach someone brand new how to play, but there are plenty of tutorials now

I've been playing this game over 2 1/2 years and will probably be playing for another 2 1/2 years, so I'd definitely recommend this game.  The more people who play, the better the matchmaking will be, and I believe the better the matchmaking is, the better the community will be since there wont be that 1 guy in the game who goes like 0/11 from being tossed to the wolves by matchmaking.

[SUMMARY]
Yet another one of those “games” that just doesn’t get the light of day, but it is truly fantastic. Free to play, quick download, and a quick “game” to work through, arguably one of the best “games” I’ve picked up in the last few weeks. Highly recommend you give this game a go, a truly enthralling tale 8.5/10
[IN-DEPTH REVIEW]
So, you are one of those people that is just not sold by my summary? Alright, here is a nice in-depth evaluation.
Oddly enough, I found myself searching through the free to play list on Steam, and sorted by popularity. I found this “game” surprising low, despite how truly amazing it is, for a game of this genre, it is truly great at what it aims to achieve. All that being said let’s get onto actually talking about the game, shall we?
First on my checklist is the storyline. The “game” being a visual novel means that it has to excel in that format, otherwise it is counter-intuitive, and that would be by no means good, would it now? The storyline itself is interesting, and I, for one, can relate. Not to having voices of the sea, but the idea of trying to trap everyone and everything out. The storyline follows a boy by the name of Cantus, not a name I can personally relate to but, is a bit out there, and is part of the reason why I remember it, it isn’t your average Bob, Phil or Vladimir, and by definition makes us as the audience be interested towards the story, maybe in hope to find out the reason of this name. This boy, is distant from society, from people to the objects around him, however, his ears are open the moment he is by the beach, and has a weird thing about liking beaches. He says a little about how he loves the sounds of the waves and how the seashells let him bring the sea home. He then meets someone on the beach, Maris, a girl, who is “slightly” older and she aims to make him smile. The game happens over 7 days, and the prologue, and if you want to know more, you are going to have to play it yourself, I personally will not be the one spoiling it for you.
Playability, as you may have noticed this “game” is not really played, it is more of a “game” where you oversee someone. Because of this factor, the “game” is being viewed, but you do have to do somethings, but fear not, this is a pick-up and play, you don’t need the controls to know what to do, the visual novel is meant to be watched rather than flat out played, and plays out somewhat in the way similar to Sakura Beach (minus those “naughty” scenes) and those games, but the net end of the storyline is always there, as far as I know there are no other endings, but as a non-owner of the DLC I can’t vouch for that. But, like I said playability, it’s easy and not really a game you play.
In terms of re-playability, since it is a visual novel, it is the standard gap in between, you may watch/play it every now and again, due to the memorable parts of the story and/or general love for the game/novel. An unfortunate problem is that, since there is no other endings, as far as my knowledge extends, there are no new experiences to gather, this loses some of the re-playability in my opinion.
That leads me to my next point, my sole complaint, is that there are no other endings, it really dampened the experience for me visual novels need to have some kind of variation of some kind, otherwise it just gets dull, and the potential fun that lies in replaying a game/novel is lost, because there is nothing else to really experiment with. That being said, the endings isn’t bad, and in fact is quite a nice ending, and day 7 wraps everything up with a nice little bow, and works well for the storyline, but at the end of the day, there just isn’t a new experience to garner from this game, besides getting the DLC (I don’t know about you, but I can’t spend that much) the game kind of gets a slight staleness from playing it again, and could turn you to hate it.
Bugs? There are none, not that I can say, good work there Zeiva Inc.
Arguably my favourite part of this novel is the graphics. The graphics, are too good to be true for this novel. The amount of time that went into them is so noticeable, the game is so flowing the graphic just go well with the storyline, if I was told to conjure up what the characters looked like from personality alone, they would look something like that (a bit more rough around the edges, I'm no Picasso), due to this I want to give a congratulations to the team for some really good graphics. They fit the tag of Anime very nicely, and I can say with confidence, that this novel is an anime. The silhouettes are also very nicely made, and add up to the feel of the game and just help massively in encasing ourselves into the world of Cantus and Maris. The graphics are so nice, I still remember them at this very moment, and they are so picturesque that it is quite astonishing, they are truly impressive, and immersive, and I love it. Also, it is run using Adobe Flash Player? Why can’t all other flash games/novel look this nice, it just really goes to show just how impressive this game really is.
The grand finale, music, sound, that lovely bundle of fun, happiness and enjoyment. The music, is just heaven, no joke. It astounds me how great it is, and how it feels part of the storyline, and is not just thrown in just so the design team can say they did something. My word, the music just goes well with the game/novel, it plays a similar role to that of the graphics which lead to the immersion, which I discussed earlier, and is part of the reason why I just keep playing on, and then put the tab open while writing this, because it’s just so peaceful, laid-back and relaxing, and like I already stated the immersion is just there for me, and even you Luke (rumour has it a Star Wars film is coming out, got to appeal to those kind of people)!
Just before I give my closing statement, I want to give a hearty congratulations to the developer on a great visual novel, and that I loved every single minute of my 60 minutes (could change) that I spend playing/watching this game/novel unfold, good work there Zeiva Inc.
So, to conclude, a heartfelt game full of passion, joy immersion and some great graphics and some catchy tunes alongside it. A truly great game, quite unique and a beautiful tale. If you are still not willing to give this game a go, then maybe you just don’t dig this kind of thing, maybe you are reading this on your phone, maybe you’re on holiday or maybe enjoying the end of school (well, for me) or getting in the Christmas spirit (it’s next week at this point in time), or perhaps you are off to Kazakhstan because, Kazakhstan is cool, no?
So, in a nutshell, good game, well played. Sorry for any mistakes, I’m not fluent English, if you have any questions, or want me to review a game, add me or drop a comment on this, or my profile. And on that bombshell…
Goodnight! (maybe it’s morning or afternoon, I don’t use clocks, way too fancy).

Ley Lines is a free game developed and published by the indie game studio Miria Studios. The concept and back story for the game revolves around the chosen of Miria cleansing corrupted crystals, making links between them, and in turn, cleansing the heart of the world.
In Ley Lines, the main chracter is in possession of a magic bow. This bow has different effects depending on what "Altar" or "Gate" she has approached or passed through last. The different effects are such as creating bubbles of reversed gravity, levitating and locking artifacts into place, as well as making bridges and slowing down time. The mechanics are all used at some point throughout the game, and all are novel and fun to play with. However, some mechanics, such as Time Slow and Teleportation are severely underused, only seeing one to three altars or gates of their kind.
The puzzles are not challenging at all and do not require a lot of brainpower to solve, but rather some precise positioning and angling sometimes, which could be considered a downfall of this game. I was frustrated more than once for just barely missing a jump, sliding down a ledge into a bottomless pit. Despite this, the puzzles are fun and novel.
About halfway through the game, it throws you a curveball by adding in enemies that spawn in artifacts and shoot them directly at you. These enemies are integral to some puzzles, and on one specific occasion I had to reload the game because the enemy decided not to respawn and I needed it to spawn me a block for use.
The only other major thing of note is the collectibles. There are 20 yellow crystals scattered throughout the in game world, and each one requires a bit of tricky manuvering or placement of your various bow shots. I managed to get 17 of them on my playthrough, I have
idea where the others could have been, and I couldnt go back to try and find them all after I completed the game.
There isnt much to say about Ley Lines in terms of Story. Only towards the end do we really get a chunk of backstory, and an explanatiuon as to why this was all happening. Frankly, while it was well executed (and very well voiced!) it felt tacked on and slightly out of place. It slowed things down, quite literally as you can't run during the final part, and was a stark change of pace from the relatively quick platforming of the main game. If there was more of an explanation from the beginning it would be more understandable, but I feel as the ending detracts from the experience and the story at large slightly.
This game is beautiful and detailed at every corner. Animations are smooth, and textures are crisp. Except for the character model's eyes. No pupils! But otherwise the game is a very wonderful visual experience. Just make sure your PC can handle it! I have a GTX950MX and it was able to only really play the game in the latter stages on the lower settings! You should be fine with a desktop class GTX960 or above, but I cannot say for sure.
The only oyher gripe I had with the game was how it handled Controller vs Mouse. At various points in the game, the UI got confused and didnt know whether or not I was playing with a mouse or a controller. It resolved itself on its own after passing through loading zones, but it was still noticible.
In a normal playthrough, you wont encounter many bugs. The game at its core runs very well and I only encountered one real hiccup throughout my experience. (See Gameplay)
Ley Lines is completely free, less than 1Gb, and is a relatively polished indie game that almost anybody can pick up and play. It hearkens back to the old platformers of the Playstation 1 era like Spyro and Crash Bandicoot, and its a welcome change of pace from all the games flaunting insane mechanics and what not.
While having it's flaws, Ley Lines is a solid first game to be published on Steam by Miria Studios. Play the game, enjoy it, and then keep an eye on the devs to see what else they have in store.

Astroneer.
First of all,
Go and show the developers of Astroneer some love:
This cute little game is a fun space exploration / survival game.
You are able to play it solo or with a friend.
Positives:
- The game is just simply gorgeous, exploring the planet/s is just gorgeous and mesmerizing. The artists have used a unique colour palette that has drawn me in.
- 4 costumes to chose from when you start a game although you cannot customise what you look like; this is good enough for me.
- You have 8 slots of space in your backpack as inventory slots, this is good for early game but it can get annoying in the late game; in late game you are able to build items to help you such as storage which then you can place items.
- Different workstations do different things which can benefit you to survive easier and for longer.
- A unique idea of surviving with oxygen where 'Tethers' will help you explore the planet and explore further from your base.
- There are storms that come randomly which throw projectiles (Rocks) around which can damage and ultimately kill you.
- The developers are constantly updating the game (Bug fixes and developing the game further).
- You can morph the environment the way you want with the object you get at the beginning of the game, which can lead to cool environments been made.
Negatives:
- The game isn't very long, so the asking price is not worth it until the developers add more to the game.
- It can be buggy at times, when improving your workstations, they can branch of inside of other workstations and this can cause a lot of confusion.
- Not much to do, as when you have built all of the vehicles and workstations there is not much else to do (relating to first point).
- The only way to save is to go to your cockpit and sit in it. So there is no quick save or save button in the menus.
- Driving the vehicles is really hard and can easily got out of control.
I recommend this game because it is a beautiful game and the developers are working really hard on this game.
Although the price is a bit steep for what you get, I know 100% that the developers will in time add in enough content for the game to be worth the full price.

I started playing this game on the 15th of August 2012, and little did I know that this game actually would be the most important game I've ever played in my life. It has given me so much. But storytime later, this is my review of the game.
Every 2 weeks they give out a new patch, which shakens up the meta, balancing and adjusting gods, items and maybe changing some of the ingame elementals on the maps, and I believe every month there is a new god to learn to play and counter. It freshens up the game every time.
There's 5 classes. Hunters, Guardians, Mages, Assassins and Warriors. Every class designed for a different role. ADC/Carry, Support, Mid, Jungle or Solo. However, it doesn't lock the classes to their designed roles. Usually you would want hunters for your carry and warriors for solo, but it doesn't say an assassin or guardian doesn't work for solo, or a mage for carry. It's all about your playstyle and how your team could work as a team and make the composition work. Every game is different for sure.
There's alot of playmodes aswell. You have conquest, the standard "Moba" map with 3 lanes, a jungle and alot of objectives. This is the most competative playmode, and also the one where professional play is involved with. Smite esport is amazing to look at, especially if you enjoy playing the game and want to see some really good teams playing against each other with different practiced tactics.
Then you have the "casual" gamemodes such as Arena, as the name states, you're basically just brawling out in a big circle with 3 different buffs on each side. Teamfights and kills are what this mode is for, but you have to watch the minions.
Assault is also here, where everyone get assigned a random god, there's just 1 lane and you can't go back into base and buy items unless you die, which also puts your team in a disadvantage for some seconds until you return stronger to lane. However, being alive for too long puts YOU at a disadvantage. All random, all mid. This is also obviously the most unbalanced gamemode where your team can lose by just the gods you are assigned with. But hey, this is made for casual fun and playing gods you probably normally would, so why would you play assault if you're just going to complain?
Then there's Clash. The "Mix between arena and conquest" which is 2 lanes, a huge buff-monster in the middle and some sidejungle with a mana buff. Quite fun, but also just really a cluster of switching between lanes and outplaying the other team.
The last "casual only" gamemode is Siege, which also is two lanes, and has a big siege-monster in middle which is assigned to the team that gets the killing blow on it. This has alot of HP and brings down towers quickly. A quite fun gamemode where it's not 5v5 as most other gamemodes, but there's 4v4. There's also MOTD, or Match Of The Day to touch on, where balance is out and there is a new gamemode on rotation with different twists.
Then you have the semi-competative gamemodes (with both Casual and Ranked involved) which is Joust and Duel. Duel is a ranked-only 1v1 gamemode where you ban out gods you don't want to play against, and it's only you to outplay the enemy. 1 lane with an objective to turn off the towers, and two buffs, mana and attack buff. It's all about outplaying.
Joust is nearly the same, it's on the same map but it's 3v3. So you, alongside two allies plays against 3 others to see who comes out victorious.
This game has so much to offer, tons of amazing skins, and a really great community, both on "famous" Smite players on Twitch, Twitter and aswell with Reddit and some groups on Facebook. Honestly, just all around the best MOBA out there to me, atleast, because it is indeed a 3rd person WASD-movement based MOBA.
This game has given me friends over the entire world and I even went from Norway to USA to live at some guys house for 2 weeks, all because of Smite. Thanks, Smite, for everything you've given, and this is definitely my all time favorite online PvP game.

played the first one and got too excited and pre purchased this one. The performance is so bad that I regret buying it. I'll change the review once the patch is up, for now, better wait for the patch or a sale before buying this one.

The short version is that if you loved Dishonored, you'll love Dishonored 2 more. If you loved the idea of Dishonored, then Dishonored 2's gonna be your jam. I hear some people are having technical issues with the game, but I'm lucky enough to have had a perfect, flawless 60fps run.
I loved Dishonored 2, playing the game as Corvo. I play on restarting it and doing an Emily playthrough soon, and I'm the kind of guy who usually only plays a game once with no plans to ever return, but for Dishonored 2, man... it feels so good to play, y'know? I spent over an hour alone in that first level, just exploring. Turns out that I didn't even find everything there was to find, despite how careful I thought I was.
In most ways, it's an improvement upon the original. I didn't really feel that the ending I got (there are many) reflected my playthrough, but man, that was a fun 13 hour run. 129 kills, 33 deaths, 450 times getting spotted. If I have one problem with the game, it's that it's a bit too easy to get spotted; I felt like the last one made it a bit easier to hide. This felt like it encouraged me to try combat more, and honestly, the combat's fun.
One of the key additions to the game is the introduction of the combat stun. It allows you to choke out enemies who discover you, so instead of just killin' someone or reloading a save the second you're caught, you can take your enemy on and continue in silence. I hear the domino power is amazing, but you don't get that as Corvo.
Also, there's this really cool feature where they let you choose NOT to gain magical powers, so you can do a pure stealth, no magic run, which is really cool of them. The amount of choice and consequence in this game is remarkable, but it's often so low key that you might not notice it.
It feels good, looks great, and runs flawlessly on my machine (i7 6700k, GTX 1070 via DVI, 16GB DDR4, installed on a Western Digital Black HD). I had one freeze, which officially makes it the best-running game I've played in 2016. Seriously, even Call of Duty at least had two crashes on me.
The game's real standout, for me, is its level design, which is brilliant. The last game was clearly held back by games consoles, but Dishonored 2 really gets to shine. The Clockwork Mansion is a level that's going to keep people talking for years, but I found a level that comes later to be even better. The Heart's been improved too--she now tells you a ton of stories for the guards; a few stories get repeated, but most of them I only encountered once in the game.
The story itself is cool--they reintroduce everythingm, so if you didn't play the last game, you probably won't need to play this one, but it helps, that's for sure.
The levels are insane. Seriously. Incredible level design. If you have any interest in level design, play Dishonored 2. Wonderful game.

Weaknesses:
1) I wish I could return to levels to get stuff I missed
2) I think they could slow down enemy attention/sharpness a bit
3) I had to rebind about half the keys

Bought the first game (Euro Truck Simulator) back in 2009 as CD-ROM version only. So no steam key for me. Played that for atleast 400 hours with  a nice G27 setup I made later on. Awsome game! Bought Euro Truck Simulator 2 on steam a couple years ago because of the DLCs and gameplay updates. If you enjoy driving around calmly with a truck in the exotic places of europe, this game is for you!
The game also has huge community support, so there are loads of custom maps to choose from, loads of vehicles, and lots of differently sized trailers. This community thing went so far that a small group of progammers started making a multiplayer system for the game. Now there are servers with thousands of players playing at the same time.
But I warn you! Beware of the multiplayer! If you like driving according to traffic rules (which means you are sensible), multiplayer is not for you! The amount of sh*t that other players have towards others is virtually non-existent, even in the world of Quantum Physics!
I remember back then when there were no cars in multiplayer, it was already quite cringy with all the kids buying the game just to troll around, get banned, and then have their parents call the programmers to demand to unban these imbeciles.
Verdict:
If you are here for the AI and mods for nice scenery and relaxing drives... A warm welcome to the community, I recommend you check out "Promods", very nice map mod. And check out youtube channels like DaSquirrelNuts, who makes videos on this game.
If you are here ONLY for the multiplayer. Be ashamed of yourself. And I am being honest. We already have enough of these trolls, we don't need anymore of them.
And finally, if you are here for both, feel free to check out VTCs that are available for recruitment, you might become part of a large friendly community.
Recommendations:
YES, for the sensible.
NO, for the trolls.

Astroneer.
First of all,
Go and show the developers of Astroneer some love:
This cute little game is a fun space exploration / survival game.
You are able to play it solo or with a friend.
Positives:
- The game is just simply gorgeous, exploring the planet/s is just gorgeous and mesmerizing. The artists have used a unique colour palette that has drawn me in.
- 4 costumes to chose from when you start a game although you cannot customise what you look like; this is good enough for me.
- You have 8 slots of space in your backpack as inventory slots, this is good for early game but it can get annoying in the late game; in late game you are able to build items to help you such as storage which then you can place items.
- Different workstations do different things which can benefit you to survive easier and for longer.
- A unique idea of surviving with oxygen where 'Tethers' will help you explore the planet and explore further from your base.
- There are storms that come randomly which throw projectiles (Rocks) around which can damage and ultimately kill you.
- The developers are constantly updating the game (Bug fixes and developing the game further).
- You can morph the environment the way you want with the object you get at the beginning of the game, which can lead to cool environments been made.
Negatives:
- The game isn't very long, so the asking price is not worth it until the developers add more to the game.
- It can be buggy at times, when improving your workstations, they can branch of inside of other workstations and this can cause a lot of confusion.
- Not much to do, as when you have built all of the vehicles and workstations there is not much else to do (relating to first point).
- The only way to save is to go to your cockpit and sit in it. So there is no quick save or save button in the menus.
- Driving the vehicles is really hard and can easily got out of control.
I recommend this game because it is a beautiful game and the developers are working really hard on this game.
Although the price is a bit steep for what you get, I know 100% that the developers will in time add in enough content for the game to be worth the full price.

played the first one and got too excited and pre purchased this one. The performance is so bad that I regret buying it. I'll change the review once the patch is up, for now, better wait for the patch or a sale before buying this one.

The short version is that if you loved Dishonored, you'll love Dishonored 2 more. If you loved the idea of Dishonored, then Dishonored 2's gonna be your jam. I hear some people are having technical issues with the game, but I'm lucky enough to have had a perfect, flawless 60fps run.
I loved Dishonored 2, playing the game as Corvo. I play on restarting it and doing an Emily playthrough soon, and I'm the kind of guy who usually only plays a game once with no plans to ever return, but for Dishonored 2, man... it feels so good to play, y'know? I spent over an hour alone in that first level, just exploring. Turns out that I didn't even find everything there was to find, despite how careful I thought I was.
In most ways, it's an improvement upon the original. I didn't really feel that the ending I got (there are many) reflected my playthrough, but man, that was a fun 13 hour run. 129 kills, 33 deaths, 450 times getting spotted. If I have one problem with the game, it's that it's a bit too easy to get spotted; I felt like the last one made it a bit easier to hide. This felt like it encouraged me to try combat more, and honestly, the combat's fun.
One of the key additions to the game is the introduction of the combat stun. It allows you to choke out enemies who discover you, so instead of just killin' someone or reloading a save the second you're caught, you can take your enemy on and continue in silence. I hear the domino power is amazing, but you don't get that as Corvo.
Also, there's this really cool feature where they let you choose NOT to gain magical powers, so you can do a pure stealth, no magic run, which is really cool of them. The amount of choice and consequence in this game is remarkable, but it's often so low key that you might not notice it.
It feels good, looks great, and runs flawlessly on my machine (i7 6700k, GTX 1070 via DVI, 16GB DDR4, installed on a Western Digital Black HD). I had one freeze, which officially makes it the best-running game I've played in 2016. Seriously, even Call of Duty at least had two crashes on me.
The game's real standout, for me, is its level design, which is brilliant. The last game was clearly held back by games consoles, but Dishonored 2 really gets to shine. The Clockwork Mansion is a level that's going to keep people talking for years, but I found a level that comes later to be even better. The Heart's been improved too--she now tells you a ton of stories for the guards; a few stories get repeated, but most of them I only encountered once in the game.
The story itself is cool--they reintroduce everythingm, so if you didn't play the last game, you probably won't need to play this one, but it helps, that's for sure.
The levels are insane. Seriously. Incredible level design. If you have any interest in level design, play Dishonored 2. Wonderful game.
Strengths:
1) Core movement
2) Level design
3) Tools
4) Graphics (running everything at max)
5) FOV slider and ability to disable mouse smoothing!
Weaknesses:
1) I wish I could return to levels to get stuff I missed
2) I think they could slow down enemy attention/sharpness a bit
3) I had to rebind about half the keys

If you haven't bought this game already, you should definitely buy it now. AND if you have the so-called "Destiny" I recommend abandoning it and getting yourself Borderlands 2.
Borderlands 2 is a huge world where you get to explore terrain, kill ♥♥♥♥, and get loot. Never has doing this same thing over and over again been so fun in any other game where you grind as well, since getting legendary items feels pretty satisfying (as well as the occasional pearlescent from the second Ultimate Vault Hunter Upgrade pack, despite half of them being garbage-tier).
Aside from the grinding, the story Borderlands 2 presents is damn good. BL2 has that type of dialogue that you can pop a couple of drinks to and laugh at with your friends, kind of like watching TV. It also presents one of the most (in my opinion) funniest and arguably best antagonist of any video game, Handsome Jack. Unlike most villains who encounter you from time to time without making communication with you between those times, Jack will constantly taunt you, which makes this kind of villain the one that actually pisses you off (in a good way).
The roster includes 6 characters, each of which are all fun to play, and 2 of which are DLC (which are worth buying). Play as Maya the Siren, and you get to lock your enemies in place, and better yet, manipulate them to fight for you. With Axton the Commando, you get yourself a rocket and bullet shooting turret that you could hide under to give you protection whilst fighting alongside it, fighting defensively in one position. With Salvador, the Spanish man that likes to shoot things, you can gunzerk and dual wield any kind of weapon, whether it be a pistol and a shotgun or two rocket launchers (as well as gain alot of your health back and increase your gunzerking with each kill you get, which is the Yipee Ki Yay skill). Play as Zer0, and you have two choices. You can invest in his "Bloodshed" skill tree and melee your enemies to oblivion with your katana, or the "Sniping" tree, which allows you to (probably) one-shot powerful bosses in the game, so long as aiming is your thing. Otherwise Salvador should be better suited.
Play as Gaige the Mechromancer, and get yourself your own mech which you can fight alongside with, as well as have ♥♥♥♥ty Star Wars Stormtrooper aim whilst drastically increasing your damage with the "Anarchy" skill. And lastly, with Krieg the Psycho, you can RELEASE THE BEAST AND GAIN YOURSELF A NEW HUGE HAND AND BUZZAXE AND TURN THE ENEMIES THAT SURROUND YOU INTO NIPPLE SALAD AND THROW BOOM ROCKS WITH THE "LIGHT THE FUSE" THINGY WHILE YOUR IN FIGHT FOR YOUR LIFE AND HAVE SO MUCH JOLLY GOOD TIMES.
11/10, this game is one of moist ones out there, definitely recommend it.

Where do I begin with this game? I first played it on console for roughtly 3000 hours, and then got it on PC when I started PC gaming. Yeah Yeah, I know this is an old game, but personally I think it is still super playable and fun. It is like a fine wine, and has gotten better with age.
As for story, you have your bad guy, wants to take over the world and what not. So it is like every other game right? Wrong. Handsome Jack is by far one of the best villians I have ever seen. He is extremely believable, likeable, and has a very strong charismatic vibe to him. Seriously if you don't like him there is something wrong. I will try to avoid spoilers as much as possible with this. As for the characters you see several old faces if you had the pleasure of playing the first installement of the series. Sadly though you only get to visit 1 location from the old one and that is a very limited sized area. I would have loved to see the old places like the Dahl Headlands and the Rust Commons with the updated graphics and gameplay from this one.
Gameplay is basically like most other FPS games, Firstperson so you cant see your character without mods. This isn't a bad thing in my opinion but i think it should have been optional to play in 3rd person. It is also an RPG with several different ways you can build your characters and set your skill points, which can change your melee or change up how your special ability works.
Your characters are Axton the commando, Zero the Assassin, Maya the siren, Salvador the gunzerker, Gaige the mechromancer, and Kreig the psycho.
Axton throws out a sentry turret.
Zero goes invisible and can deal out 1 stupidly powerful attack.
Maya locks 1 enemy out of the fight for a short time.
Savador pulls out a second weapon and lays waste to the enemies.
Gaige Summons her trusty rusty deathtrap.
and Kreig goes into a blood thirsty rampage.
OK so I want to make it clear that Gaige and Kreig are DLC characters so you have to pay for them.
The DLC maps are tons of fun and by far my favorite is The Assault on Dragon's Keep.

of hours to complete. Grinding like that is definitely not what makes this game fun.

[h]A bleak, empty, space exploration, and world crafting sandbox game.[/h]

is a MOBA-style game with a unique take on an oversaturated genre with Gods of various ancient mythologies taking center stage. Rather than the traditional top-down perspective of most MOBAs SMITE decides to make the gameplay up-close and personal by taking things 3rd person with a more action oriented control scheme. It offers all the traditional modes you know and love (Conquest, ARAM, etc) with also some new modes like the fast paced arena mode or 3v3 Joust. What seperates SMITE from the others is (at least to me) it's more casual friendly focus on fun and action over intense number crunching and sometimes stale matches. Which is probably why the most popular modes in SMITE would have to be Arena, ARAM and Joust. This may turn away some people, but i've been playing since early beta and since im still around, i think it has more than enough depth and fun-factor to keep you playing for a while.
+ Character designs are detailed and interesting
+ Many fun modes to choose from
+ Good for beginners new to the genre
+ Tons of Gods to choose from (You can even buy the whole pack!)
+ Great amount of awesome skins, voice packs, and icons.
- Community is rather small compared to DOTA2 or LOL
- Community is filled with newbies and toxic/abusive players
- Wonky Matchmaking can really mess up your day
Hi-Rez does nothing to punish toxic players.
Give it a shot! Some people may like SMITE for it's colorful action-packed 3rd person gameplay, and others may rather stick with the competition. While it does have it's problems i do enjoy it for being just different enough to give you a break from the more serious and popular MOBA games. SMITE to me is all about a good time, and most of the time, it is.

A note/update to everyone having optimazation issues with the game, and also those disliking my review simply because I've actually played the damn thing instead of complaining about my computer not running it well: Wait for a patch, get better hardware, or just turn down the settings and stop complaining. It's really that simple. Get over yourselves. Granted, I may just be lucky that my game works completely fine, but I honestly doubt it.
I have mid-range hardware and I can play as expected, with almost no issue. I honestly don't understand all the negativity the game is getting, simply for its optimization. Yes, the optimization could be a lot better, but frankly, I wouldn't have even noticed performance issues without the constant complaining. With a 970, I run the game at hgh settings, 1080p, 60 fps. Sometimes the fps goes as low as 40, when the game is literally loading 2 entirely different maps simultaneously (That mission is damn awesome btw), but its still playable by all means. I feel that people are being needlessly negative, acting as if the game is unplayable simply because they wanted flawless 2K gameplay. If you get around the fact that the optimization is simply mediocre, the game is astounding. Stunning graphics, solid characters, great voice acting, AND AMAZING GAMEPLAY AND STORY. If I were to have one gripe, I would say that it feels just a tad too much like the orginal, but really only if you play as Corvo. But to be frank, the first game was so great that I barely mind it. And one thing I REALLY love is how much sheer replayability the game has. There are essentially 8 solid, vastly different umbrella ways to play between Corvo and Emily, utilizing stealth, assault, lethal, and nonlethal variations and choices. All in all, if you enjoyed Dishonored in the slightest, you'll love this game, regardless of all the people complaining about performance. As a note though, just make sure you're close to the reccomended specs, and you can play just fine. Otherwise, just turn down the settings and either wait for a patch, and stop pointlessly complaining  ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

A real treat if you were born in the 80's and like Anime. An absolute gift for those who were born in the 80's, like Anime and grew up in Latin America.
Games like this gem are really hard to come across. It's Fan Service in its most pure form. The first one 'Brave Soldiers' was a surprise, but this second one still makes me feel like if it was just a dream. Everything that we know and love from the classic Saint Seiya is there. All Bronze saints with their respective armor version, plus unarmored and many other variants from the show, including God Cloths. All Gold Saints; as with Bronze Saints, also including various variants, plus God Cloths from the newly released 'Soul of Gold' Anime. Asgard God Warrios... So I have to say more? ASGARD!. Marina Generals, as expected, as well as the main folks from the Hades arc. There are a few other interesting characters added in that are very welcome. Really, everything is here.
And in an even greater twist, the Mexican dub artists from the original Latin America dub gave their voices for the Spanish in-game audio option. I mean... What else can you freaking ask for?!
Fanboysm apart, let's focus on the game.
The game pretty much feels like the first one, but there has been some changes and improvements made. It is still a super-basic fighting game, that anyone can pick up in a few minutes. It's definitely not a pure-breed competitive fighting game, but it is not what it's meant for I feel. Most people playing this game will be old folks like me, reliving fights from the anime, while using our imagination to bring back those amazing memories.
Graphics are amazing. I mean, not ground-breaking, but they are bright, colorful, models are well designed and animated, and the Ultimate cutscenes will give you goosebumps. The game does run a lot better on PC than in PS4 (version that I also have).  You get 60fps and overal better resolution. Which does, unfortunately, make some low-rew textures a bit more obvious than in the console.
Overal an amazing gift from Namco Bandai. This game was obviously not going to be popular, or worth noting for players not familiar with Saint Seiya, but still, not only they took the time to make a game, but also an even more amazing sequel.
Things like these, games made with love dedicated to a specific fanbase are a rare sight these days. Thanks to the developers.

For example, Michael Stackpole cut his creative teeth on this game.  Let that sink in for a second.   Michael F#|<ing Stackpole, the guy who went on to write novels and such? Your mind may even explode like a blood sausage.  But trust me, that's a good thing.

I used to love playing  this on my old Apple 2e. Me and my friends would huddle around the computer and play coop before it even existed. Each of us created unique characters inside of Ranger Station slamming on the SPACEBAR forever to roll up the best stats and get the best points. We essentially would play cooperatively on 1 computer where we would take turns actually using the computer. The player would type and move around, while the other people simply watched the game and spoke aloud what they wanted their characters to do. "Attack, Burst, Leather Thug to the left". "Disband, move up." This last statement our close combat character would literally say 100 times each session. It  was all part of the fun, and while it sounds  painful, it was actually a blast. We'd make our party consisting of a "gun guy", a "brawler", a "doc", and a "nerd".
The gun guy we'd load up with gun skills like SMG and Assault Rifle (M1989A1 NATOs baby!) and AT Weapon, this guy was clutch for making sure he shot and actually hit stuff in the game, where even if you have a really good DEX stat you might not hit what you shoot unless you take the skill too.
The brawler would get pugilism and melee weapon skills (basically a tank in close quarter combat) and of course he'd get dibs on the Manglers and Clubs and stuff. Of course he never really relied only on melee and could take out some punks at a distance with a .45 or whatever. The doc is well, a medic with loads of Medic skill and a ridiculous INT stat, and the nerd was a well-rounded character that had a maximum INT but took skills that were not medic; forgery, metallurgy, lockpick, etc.
I can't tell you how many hours of my life I spent huddled in front of the glow of my color composite monitor swapping disks playing Wasteland. It is a brutally difficult game by todays standards with permadeth period. No options for ressurection unless you save your game ahead of time, when you die you're dead. Perhaps part of what made this game so compelling to me and my friends was that we actually had to focus, use our brains for team work, and have a strategy instead of just mindless button mashing like we were doing on our NESes with Rush'n'Attack, Rygar, and Ikari Warriors (among others). We would die often and we would regroup and rethink of our strategy. We would pick better skills learn more about the attributes and when they played a role and for what and this whole time we were actually having a boatload of fun. I can remember TPD (total party death) once we reached Las Vegas ♥♥♥♥♥♥I remember this happening in Quartz too, the game is freaking hard and the deck is definitely not stacked in your favor) as we got shredded to pieces by a cyborg with energy weapons (up until then we didn't even know energy weapons existed). It took hours to rebuild, start over, and level up to be strong enough to get back to Las Vegas and actually take those bots down.
We used to build 4 characters in Ranger Station, only 1 of which would we actually try to make decent. This character was the "courier" he would be escorting the cannon fodder other 3 characters straight to Quartz, where they would sell EVERY piece of gear they owned, then he'd Pool the money and walk them back to Range Station, and we'd delete them. Do this 100 - 300 times, and you can amass an enormous cache of weapons, armor, money, etc. Then when  you have your loot and gear all sorted, you build 3 other characters and you give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about them too. After those 3, we would give the couriers♥♥♥♥♥♥to another remaning character either kill the courier to create a better character, or sometimes we'd just keep him. We used macros to automate most of this. In essence, this is cheating against the spirit of the game, but it was ♥♥♥♥ing  hard and we were young and thought we were clever. I can tell you even then it wasn't always easy after. Yes we might have SMG's and NATO Assault rifles with boatloads of clips and TNT and Kevlar armor, but we still got our asses handed to us in Vegas.
We got ver close to beating the game, but we could never find the Sleeper Base to make it to space.
I know, right? It' s pretty old, and it doesn't age super well. If you didn't grow up playing this game you might hate it. If you can get past the old-ness of the game, the graphics even with this re-release are not great, the SA antialiasing helps, but I kinda like the crunchy pixels better. The music and the voice overs are pretty awesome in this version; we had a paragraph book we'd use to read from (which doubled as a form of copy protection).
If you like oldschool RPGs that are top-down (like Ultima, or 2400AD) and you are ready to commit to actually trying to win (if that's your thing) and don't mind getting your♥♥♥♥♥whipped until you learn some tricks and techniques, this game will reward you.
There is a lot of game in ths small package, and there is a lot of personality and character that this game had that no other game did. EA innovated on many fronts with Wasteland, and not just in the computer but the paragraphs really added a ton of story and immersion to the game that other RPGs of the time lacked sorely. It was like living in the best "Choose Your Own Adventure" (don't get be started about how awesome those books were in my childhood) computer game ever made.
If you're a fan of Fallout at all, you will probably like this game. It takes time and dedication, but this is the precursor to all the others. For that reason alone you should check it out, but the game has tons of merit as well, and the re-release really does try to polish an old title to a more modern standard. I think it does a pretty good job, but I had some issues getting the mouse to work. The keyboard is the way to go and it works no problem.
You needed an imagination in the old days, and you still need it today, but the voice overs really do help make this game a lot better than it was. The music is OK too. Is it going to blow your mind? Probably not. Is it going to keep you coming back, maybe. Is it going to make you work for the reward of the story? Without a doubt.
Wasteland is one of my favorite games and I highly recommend it.

As someone who has playing for about a year with almost 400+ hours stored up, I feel I need to clear some bad rep. The game does have its faults, and the market system can seem a bit jacked up, but people fail to try to look at the good things compared to the bad.
Cons:
The matchmaking should be improved as well as server regulation of high threat levels. Also, it should be made aware that some people learn faster than others, so don't just think that just because someone keeps owning you, that you suck or he is cheating.
Tutorials and game information needs to be much more accessible and easier to understand and more in-depth than current ones. The tutorials should also give some explanation to threat levels and how the game mechanics work.
Community support should be taken more into consideration. I'm not saying the developers do whatever the community tells them they need to do, but the community needs to be better considered, and developers need to explain that they are doing their best and it takes lots of time to make code and system changes in the game.
The armas marketplace needs to make pricing a bit more fair and cheaper, as well as maybe allowing permanent guns available through contacts. Also, it may help to point out that it could be better if they allowed some sort of G1C to in-game cash converter so the social marketplace is more fair, as well as maybe a player trade option.
Finally, the game should try to support VAC since they can help ban people who truly need to be banned.
Pros:
It's considered a p2w, but if think about it, its really a pay-to-develop or pay-to-play, since the devs need lots of money to pay their people. It takes about 6 months to make a system code change, and that can only be done be a certain individual, so cut the guys some slack.
Customization, if done appropriately, can lead to numerous different styles and expressions of personalities, beliefs, or to their liking. Plus, the game's cars and guns are balanced for every play style and tactic out there.
There are some people, like myself, that are willing to offer help to new players, and are willing to bestow our knowledge to help the player not feel like that every mission is a pain in the neck. Also, the clan system can really help a new player, as most clans are around to help new players get started, or to provide a sense of hospitality and friendship to those who need it in this game.
The guns in the armas marketplace and the legendary weapons in joker boxes are not OP or p2w guns. Some are mod-able re-skins of in-game weapons like the joker cr5 to the ntec-5 or the ump is to the pmg. Also, just because a high rank or new player has a VBR "huntress" or a Medusa doesn't mean he paid money to buy it, cause some people save up millions of in-game cash to actually buy the gun.
Also, the replay value of the game is massive, especially if you only played as an enforcer or criminal to max rank. There will be days when you feel down cause you can't seem to win a mission, and days that you feel like a champ for doing better than normal, but it's really worth it. If you look up and know how the game works, and listen to experienced players' advice, you will be coming back for a good time.

If you're like me, a Saint Seiya fan since your childhood and never got to play any games because they were all from consoles you didn't own, you probably don't care about reviews and is going to buy anyway...
Nevertheless, here are some thing to keep in mind, based on my experience:
-No major problems on how the game runs
-The fighting mechanics are great, definitely one of the greatest aspects of the game
-The story format is very nice and brings that nostalgia of watching the anime back in the days. However...
-That feeling soons crumbles when faced with the sort of lazy and cheap visual structure of the game. Basically the story is reenacted by placing the characters on one of the stages without properly integrating the two, which makes it feel like the characters are out of place, with awkward motions and sort of lifeless. A lot of other BANDAI fighting games have the same problem, but in Saint Seiya: Soldier's Soul it becomes more evident, maybe because of my hype for this game, or Saint Seiya being not a as popular franchise, leading to more development restrictions (budget, staff, deadlines and such)
-The stages look poorly done, unpolished. the characters are pretty good, the fighting is smooth, which makes the flaws in the stages stand out even more. Don't get me wrong, the places are more or less well represented, but still give off a "We don't have any more time or money to work on this" vibe. This doesn't make much difference during the fighting, it's more of an issue for cutscenes.
Overall, the initial experience is somewhat disappointing, as the flaws in the game promptly show up, but as you play you can get past them and enjoy the actual gameplay with a great fighting experience. With these considerations, I recommend the game for anyone, even if you're not a Saint Seiya fan. You just might want to wait for the game to be on sale, though.

Saint Seiya was a magnificient anime series in the 80s, and a personal favourite as a kid. It never had any great game and while SSSS (so many S's) is not the definitive Saint Seiya game that breaks this curse, it is certainly a step forward to bring a decent title to their fans.
Saint Seiya: Soldiers Soul is a Dimps fighting game. For those having played any Naruto or One Piece iterations of the title, you know the drill: simple fighting game mechanics that focus more on bringing an enormous quantity of characters and flashy attacks more than a deep system at all. Regrettably and when compared to their predecessors, SS:SS seems like a lazy attempt to emulate this formula in a Saint Seiya game, with subpar graphics, almost clonic characters and not much depth into the system. There are a couple of good ideas here and there, but nothing too cutting-edge.
At any rate: in SS:SS, you will be able to revisit the main arcs of the Saint Seiya series: the Sanctuary Arc, Poseidon Arc, Asgaard Arc and Hades Arc. While the story will keep you interested and it gets less repetitive than it should thanks to the constant switching of characters for canon issues. After you complete the story, there are a couple more modes that provide some challenge, but at the point I had completed tha main story, I could barely feel any interesting on keeping up with the game (aside from vs modes).
In conclusion, I think this game is a good buy for Saint Seiya hardcore fans at most. If you are looking for a fighting game, there are much better options in Steam. And if it's anime fighting games that you dig, I think the Naruto or One Piece options are way better. BTW, be sure to grab a gamepad as the controls are much better implemented than in a keyboard.
Overall I give this game a 6/10

As others have noted there are occasional glitches in the graphics - low frame rate and such.  However they are seldom, and to condemn a game outright for an issue that's liable to be fixed in the first patch is idiotic.  There aren't any SYSTEMATIC problems - just fine tuning.  I say that up front to just get it out of the way.
Beyond that, there aren't any issues to speak of.  As games go these days, getting one with so FEW issues is kind of like a cool breeze on a hot day.  You just wish it would last forever.  Kudos to Arkane for not spinning out under the pressure.  Good job, guys.  Predictably, the 'serious' gamers who think lots of power is a panacea are whining that doesn't play like a rigged demo at top resolution.  Suck it up, princesses.  I don't even have to liquid-cool this thing and the game works fine.
There are a number of puzzles.  I'm still working on some of the solutions, but some of them are positively fiendish.  Of course, if you've played Dishonored, you're familiar with this.  It's one of the game's draws. What's even better is it still PLAYS like Dishonored.  So many times original games get a sequel and the entire feel of the game goes sideways.  This is Dishonored, alright.  A few new things, a few fixed bad old things, a stack of new content and story-lines, but there's no mistaking the game.  Thanks for that, Arkane.  What worried me most was that I was paying for something that would turn out to be other than what I bought - like paying for a new watch and finding out it looks almost exactly like a sauce pan.
There are a few things that I still don't care for much , but they've always been part of Dishonored, so it's part of the feel of the game. I've come to regard them as bonus challenges, so if you want to do it the hard way, it's REALLY hard.  It's things like that that kept me coming back to the original.  It doesn't matter how many times you've played, there is always something else.
I dare not say much more for fear of spoilers, but if you liked the original - buy this.  If you didn't play the original - buy this anyway.  You'll doubtless find yourself picking up the original, too.  If you didn't like the original, well, there's no accounting for bad taste.
I would really like to experience this game. But I'll stick to the first Dishonored since its playable.

Some of the enemy detection is ridiculous too. I had one guard who was actually looking in the opposite direction of me suddenly detect me. I was totally hidden and standing still. Guards can also spot you hiding from a great distance, yet some right next to you can't see you at all; this all makes the immersion and realism suffer. I can handle difficult stealth, but not when it's unrealistic or ridiculous. I'm only 5 hours into the game so hopefully it may improve, but at the moment I'm very tempted to replay as Emily just to bring some novelty into the game compared to the original.
As for the graphics, they aren't really that much better than the original at times. As other reviewers have mentioned, the lighting seems to be over exposed and washed out, and there seems to be a blurriness to all the textures, especially if you widen your FOV.
I'd recommend the game purely because it's Dishonored, but if you've played the original then you might be disappointed.

StuntMANIA Reloaded was a game which I had conflicting thoughts on. It's fun and not serious or a pretentious game, and it feels like it was developed with attention and good intentions, however it has a few drawbacks which stopped it being as good as it could have been.
+ The design is mostly consistent throughout, nothing feels out of place
+ Controls mostly work well
+ A throwback to games such as Re-volt, and more of a unique game today
+ The aesthetics, environment design and the car models are well designed and make the game quite visually appealing and colourful
+ The sound design is pretty good and the soundtrack is fun to listen to, nothing special or memorable but it works and it isn't particularly annoying or makes you want to turn the sound off. The engine noises sound like the cars actually have power behind them and each vehicle seems to have different sounds.
Negatives
- As other reviews stated, it's pretty glitchy. Most of these aren't game-breaking but some of them get pretty annoying, such as respawning in mid air and being thrown around or having small areas of ground which aren't solid.
- The car handling seems to be pretty strange, quite slippery until you collect power-ups, it seems to improve a little then but it's still quite odd.
- One level glitched and didn't have any sound playing, the sewer level glitched and some areas were without light, making it pitch black and impossible to see where you were.
-The collectables don't seem to have any purpose other than the coins, which could have been done better so that you had more of a reason to collect them.
- You can't see how many collectables you've picked up until you collect another one, making it difficult to tell later on in the level if you've collected everything.
- The game doesn't end when you collect everything so you have to manually end the game which feels strange. There's no indicator of if you've played a level before besides having unlocked it.
That said, I bought this in a bundle for cheap and it ended up being one of the better games of the bundle, and it made up for the cost of the bundle by itself.

While other rpgs of the era had you running around dungeons slaying rats and fighting generic evil wizards or abusing the limited memory of the game as you ransacked villages of innocent people only to leave and kill them all again, Wasteland was setting a new trend of making your choices count and forcing you to live with them. No clerics to raise your dead back to life, no instant magical healing and no one to hold your hand and tell you where to go. Wasteland had no qualms about letting you try to go where you please and if you could survive then by all means break the sequence and go exploring.
The storyline may seem simple compared to gems that came a decade later, but it still stands up far better than most other rpgs of its era and indeed a good deal of the ones we've seen today. It was hard, it was unforgiving, it expected you to think and take your own notes and it was great, this is what rpgs were in the late 80s and it's defintely not for everyone especially if you've been raised on modern games the whole time you've been playing.
But, if you're patient, if you can look beyond 16 color Enhanced Graphics Adapter art, if you can handle having to read things and keep track of information on your own, then maybe, just maybe you're cut out to be a Desert Ranger.

Just bare in mind that it's not going to wow you, and you will have to print out a reference card and potentially the entire manual to properly understand the controls and storyline.

That said? If you know what you're getting yourself into, Wasteland still holds the hell up and is full of its own crazy charm. I'D recommend turning off the new graphics, just because the vectorization filter it puts on everything drives me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but if you dig it, don't let me stop you. This game was produced a while back and was intended for the Xbox 360. So if you don't have an older controller or one that adapts to the Xbox 360, you will have a hard time controlling your character. I purchased a Hori Fighting Commander for Street Fighter V, but ended up using it for this game. The controller has a switch.
At first, I was frustrated because the character would not respond to the input on my Hori Pro Kai 4. Then the buttons were in the wrong configuration. Forget about customer service from Namco-Bandai. They are worthless and clearly state that there is no longer support for this game.
Battle mode - nobody online to play against.
Storyline - the best part of the game. Just play your way through all the stages. It tends to get tedious as the game play is the same because the characters movements are limited within a confined stage. Yes, the stage has borders.
Continues are ridiculous... you have to slam the buttons so fast while Athena tries to wake you up. Better off dying (countdown expires) and then pressing start button again. Unlimited continues.
So far, I've played through 3 of the story-arcs. I've stopped at Hades. Because of time and boredom. The game gets tedious at times and sometimes, you really don't want to play as Cygnus. Phoenix Ikki is the best IMO. I think this is a great game to have in your library despite the setbacks, but definitely don't pay more than $15. Not worth $49.99. Better to wait for a sale or find the key on another website.

Extremely boring. Avoid.

I'm not sure if a game like this can still be appreciated in these modern days of fancy 3D graphics and short attention spans... but it damn well should be. For whatever my opinion may be worth, I hereby go on record to state that this is one of the greatest RPGs ever made. Of course, that bold statement does come with a couple of caveats: first, my thoughts may very well be colored by nostalgia to a fair degree; and second, I haven't actually played this game in over 20 years, so it's entirely possible I am just forgetting all the bad parts. At any rate, if you are into RPGs, classic games, or at all interested in revisiting the early days of PC gaming, this is one of the very few games that should be near the top of anyone's "must-play someday" list. While I can't guarantee playing this game will captivate and inspire you the same way it did for people back in the day, I am at least fairly confident that the game itself is probably fundamentally solid, even if the underlying technology and graphics don't hold up. So definitely give this a look if you're open to embracing "the classics", or if you're just an old man like me pining for the good old days.

ASTRONEER is a sandboxish open world game, set in space (go figure). You are flung onto a planet with nothing but a spacesuit, a backpack, a deformer and a habitat to resupply you with oxygen. (Side note - developers, if you read this, could you make the stock oxygen tank last longer? A single minute is really difficult to start off with.) Leaving the safety of the habitat, you need to gather resources to expand and build modules, create vehicles, etc. Your Deformer tool is like a multi-purpose pickaxe - destroy or build upon the natural world and flatten the land. Instead of Minecraft/terraria/starbound building (which is block-based), each and every part of the natural, mouldable ground is made of triangular prisms, and using the deformer tool removes or adds these prisms to the rest of the world, which is actually amazing and I congratulate the devs on making a game that could have been a simple Minecraft rip-off, but doing so much more. You could have made it cubic, but you made this actual masterpiece.
The game, being in early access, can do with some smoothing out. Here are a couple things I reckon could be a good addition to the game.
-Backpack and storage - maybe its me, but I think there could be more options for storage. When you start the game, the backpack size is enough, but as you progress, storage becomes a bit tedious. I've heard that you can get storage with 8 slots, but maybe make another storage option with 16 storage slots?
-Vehicles - maybe this is just me, but I feel that the vehicles are a bit floaty. It happens to flip over a lot for me. Also (this is a graphical thing) if the rover has infinite oxygen from it, shouldn't the rover have a closed cockpit? Just visual things.
-Building - Building so far is great, if you just want a purely operational base. Here are some things I reckon could make the building feel better and easier, and cooler.
1) Make it so you can put modules underground from another module/habitat that is aboveground. I have a underground cave to serve as vehicle storage and safe haven from flying debris from storms.
2) Maybe you can build big habitats? I'm thinking large circular things which you can go into and walk around inside that have oxygen inside of them. Think if there were people on Mars, they would have something to go into.
3)Solar panel modules - I don't know if these are actually in the game, but what if modules you can turn into large modules. To go with that, what about battery modules too.
4) In terms of actually using the deformer tool, maybe you could hold a key down that makes the radius of the deformer tool a lot smaller? Because doing fine things is intensely difficult currently.
Maybe its the weather today, maybe its because the game is set in space (mostly because the game is set in space), maybe because I like the open world sandboxing (that too) but this game really appeals to me. I encourage anyone who has a spare $20 to buy this game, and watch as it (hopefully) turns into something even greater than it is right now.

I really love the Saint Seiya series, so I had to purchase this game after I missed the PS3 releases. Graphics are really good and reminiscent of the anime. Even the cut-scenes are excerpts from the anime, but in a vector-polygon style. The game takes you through the storyline as if you were watching the anime.
This game was produced a while back and was intended for the Xbox 360. So if you don't have an older controller or one that adapts to the Xbox 360, you will have a hard time controlling your character. I purchased a Hori Fighting Commander for Street Fighter V, but ended up using it for this game. The controller has a switch.
At first, I was frustrated because the character would not respond to the input on my Hori Pro Kai 4. Then the buttons were in the wrong configuration. Forget about customer service from Namco-Bandai. They are worthless and clearly state that there is no longer support for this game.
Battle mode - nobody online to play against.
Storyline - the best part of the game. Just play your way through all the stages. It tends to get tedious as the game play is the same because the characters movements are limited within a confined stage. Yes, the stage has borders.
Continues are ridiculous... you have to slam the buttons so fast while Athena tries to wake you up. Better off dying (countdown expires) and then pressing start button again. Unlimited continues.
So far, I've played through 3 of the story-arcs. I've stopped at Hades. Because of time and boredom. The game gets tedious at times and sometimes, you really don't want to play as Cygnus. Phoenix Ikki is the best IMO. I think this is a great game to have in your library despite the setbacks, but definitely don't pay more than $15. Not worth $49.99. Better to wait for a sale or find the key on another website.
